あ.etymology: Primary native Japanese vocalic interjection expressing sudden realization, surprise, or response, attested from Old Japanese texts (including the Kojiki and Man'yōshū) onward.

history.meaning: exclamation of emotion or sudden notice

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — あ

ああ.etymology: Long-vowel native Japanese interjection formed by lengthening あ, attested since classical literature for deep emotion, sighing, realization, or calm agreement ('ah, yes').

history.meaning: exclamation of grief, admiration, or sighing
interjection of realization, agreement, or reflection

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ああ

ああっ.etymology: Emphatic glottalized variant of the interjection ああ, with final っ representing a sudden glottal stop triggered by alarm, startle, or urgent realization.

history.meaning: abrupt exclamation of startle or sudden realization

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ああ

あげる.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) verb 上げる, continuing Old Japanese *agu* ('to raise, lift up'). From raising an offering to a social superior ('humbly give'), it bleached in modern speech into the general polite verb for giving.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 上げる

あっ.etymology: Short glottalized exclamation built on the interjection あ with a final glottal stop (っ), marking an instantaneous flash of notice, surprise, or remembering.

history.meaning: sharp interjection of sudden notice or surprise

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — あっ

あと.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ato* ('footprint, track, wake, behind'), attested in the Man'yōshū. From spatial 'tracks left behind', it extended to 'what follows behind in space or time' ('after, later, remainder').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 後

あなた.etymology: Compound of the distal demonstrative root あ ('yon, that over there') and かた / なた ('direction, side'), originally a spatial noun ('over there, beyond'). In Early Modern Japanese (Edo period), indirect reference to a respected person 'on yonder side' became a polite second-person pronoun ('you').

history.meaning: yonder direction; over there; third person

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 貴方

あの.etymology: Adnominal demonstrative formed from the distal deictic root あ ('that over there, shared in memory') and the genitive/attributive particle の. Also used as a conversation-opening hesitation filler ('um, excuse me').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — あの

あら.etymology: Native Japanese exclamation attested from Old and Early Middle Japanese for surprise or emotion; in Early Modern and Modern Japanese it became particularly associated with mild surprise or gentle notice ('oh my').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — あら

ありがたい.etymology: Compound adjective formed in Old/Early Middle Japanese from the continuative stem あり (from ある 'to exist, be') + かたし / がたい (難い 'hard, difficult'). Originally meaning 'rare, hard to come by', Buddhist usage shifted the sense toward 'precious, blessed, inspiring gratitude', yielding modern 'grateful, welcome'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 有り難い
Wiktionary — ありがたい (有り難い) (Japanese)

ありがとう.etymology: Polite greeting of gratitude derived by *u*-onbin (sound euphony) from ありがたく (adverbial form of ありがたい 'rare, precious, appreciated'), shortened from expressions such as ありがとうございます ('it is a rare/blessed thing').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 有り難う
Wiktionary — ありがとう (有り難う) (Japanese)

ありがとうございます.etymology: Formed from the adjective 有り難い (*arigatai*, from 有り 'exist' + 難い 'hard, difficult': 'rare, precious, hard to come by') via the *-ku > -u* adverbial sound change (*arigataku* > *arigatō*) plus polite ございます.

history.form: ありがとうございます

sources.title: Wiktionary — ありがとうございます (Japanese)

ある.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ari* ('to exist, be present, have'), an irregular *r*-stem (*ra-hen*) verb attested throughout the earliest eighth-century texts. In modern Japanese it serves as the standard verb of inanimate existence and possession.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 有る

あれ.etymology: Distal demonstrative pronoun built on the deictic root あ ('yon, that over there') + pronominal suffix -れ. Already replacing older かれ for distant visible objects by the late Heian and Kamakura periods; also used as an exclamation of surprise ('huh?').

history.meaning: that one (distal pronoun); exclamation of puzzlement

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — あれ

あれっ.etymology: Colloquial glottalized interjection derived from the demonstrative/interjection あれ with a sharp final glottal stop (っ), expressing sudden puzzlement or noticing something unexpected ('huh?, wait a second!').

history.meaning: abrupt exclamation when noticing something odd

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — あれ

いい.etymology: Colloquial modern Tokyo/standard form of the adjective よい (良い 'good'), arising in Edo-period eastern Japanese via vowel assimilation (*yoi* > *ii*). Conjugated inflections (よく, よかった, etc.) still retain the historical よ- stem.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — いい

いいえ.etymology: Polite negative response interjection ('no') that emerged in Early Modern Japanese by lengthening and compounding earlier negative/corrective exclamations いや / いえ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — いいえ

いかが.etymology: Phonological development in Heian-period Early Middle Japanese from Old Japanese *ikani ka* (いかにか 'in what manner?, how?'), via nasalization and voicing (*ikanika* > *ikaga*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 如何

いくつ.etymology: Interrogative number word formed in Old Japanese from the interrogative root いく- ('how many, what extent') and the native numeral classifier suffix -つ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 幾つ

いける.etymology: Potential verb derived from いく (行く 'to go, proceed well'), attested from the Edo period onward in the idiomatic senses 'can go', 'works well', 'tastes good', or 'can handle alcohol'. Also writes 生ける / 活ける ('to arrange flowers') from the transitive verb meaning 'keep alive'.

history.meaning: be able to go; be passable or tasty
can go; be good/doable; work well

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 行ける

いたす.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *itasu* (致す), originally meaning 'to cause to arrive, bring about, carry through to the end' (causative counterpart of 至る *itaru* 'to reach'). From medieval Japanese onward it grammaticalized into the humble verb for 'to do'.

history.meaning: bring to a destination; bring about

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 致す

いたた.etymology: Spontaneous exclamation of physical pain ('ouch, ow!') formed by partial reduplication of the stem いた- of the adjective 痛い (いたい 'painful, aching').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 痛い

いただきます.etymology: Polite mealtime and receiving formula, the *-masu* form of いただく (頂く 'to place on top of one's head; humbly receive'). Originally referring to the gesture of raising a gift or bowl toward the crown of the head (頂 *itadaki*) in gratitude before partaking.

history.meaning: hold aloft on the crown of the head
I humbly receive (said before eating or accepting)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頂きます

いただける.etymology: Potential form of the humble verb いただく (頂く 'to humbly receive'), used in polite modern Japanese to ask or state whether one 'can receive' a favor or action ('could I have you do...').

history.meaning: be able to humbly receive; could you please

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頂ける

いっぱい.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一杯 (いっぱい), from 一 ('one') + 杯 ('cup, vessel, bowlful'). From 'one full cup', it broadened in Early Modern Japanese to 'filled to capacity' and colloquially 'a lot, many'.

history.meaning: full to the brim; a lot; many

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一杯

いつ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *itu* ('when, what time'), built on the interrogative root *i-* (shared with いずこ, いかに, いく) plus temporal suffix *-tu*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 何時

いつも.etymology: Compound adverb formed from the temporal interrogative いつ ('when') and the inclusive particle も ('even, every'), literally 'at every when' -> 'always, usually'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 何時も

いとこ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *itoko* (従兄弟 / 従姉妹), attested in the Man'yōshū as a term of endearment ('beloved person, dear one', likely from *ito* 'very, dearly' + *ko* 'child/person') and kinship term for a cousin.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 従兄弟

いや.etymology: Conversational negative or corrective interjection/conjunction ('no, wait, well') continuing earlier Japanese いや (否 'no'), alongside the homophonous adjective/noun 嫌 (いや 'disagreeable, reluctant', from Old Japanese *iya*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 嫌

いやあ.etymology: Expressive lengthened form of the interjection いや, used in spoken Japanese when expressing bashfulness, relief, admiration, or conversational hesitation ('well now, oh boy').

history.meaning: lengthened exclamation of modesty, surprise, or warmth

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — いやあ

いらっしゃいませ.etymology: Standard welcoming greeting in shops and inns, formed from いらっしゃい (imperative/continuative of the honorific verb いらっしゃる 'to come, go, be') + polite imperative auxiliary ませ (from ます).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — いらっしゃいませ
Wiktionary — いらっしゃいませ (Japanese)

いらっしゃる.etymology: Honorific verb ('to come, go, or be') developed in Edo-period Japanese by phonological contraction from いらせられる (iraserareru), itself built from 入る (iru 'to enter/go') + causative-honorific suffixes -(さ)せ + -られる.

history.form: いらせられる (入らせられる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — いらっしゃる

いる.etymology: Spelled ゐる (wiru) prior to modern kana reform. Originally meaning 'to sit down' or 'stay still in one spot' in contrast with standing, it broadened into the standard verb of animate existence ('be present, stay') and progressive aspect.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 居る

う.etymology: Classical and modern volitional/presumptive auxiliary suffix (*-u*), which arose in Early Middle Japanese via loss of intervocalic *-m-* from Old Japanese tentative/volitional suffix *-mu* (む): *-amu* > *-au* > *-ō*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — う

うう.etymology: Primary vocalic groaning or pondering interjection representing a low closed-lip or back-vowel vocalization when straining, enduring pain, or hesitating.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — うう

ううっ.etymology: Glottalized variant of うう with a sudden final catch in the throat (っ), representing a suppressed groan, sudden wince, or choked emotion.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — うう

うそ.etymology: Native Japanese noun 嘘 (うそ 'lie, falsehood, fib'), attested from the Muromachi period onward. Often linked etymologically to older *uso* ('whistling, blowing breath') or to *oso* ('careless, false, foolish' in Old Japanese *osoro*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 嘘

うち.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *uti* (内 'inside, interior, enclosure'). From 'interior space', it came to denote one's own household or home (家), one's in-group, and temporal 'within, while'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 内

うっかり.etymology: Mimetic adverb with the *-ri* adverbial suffix on an older root *uka-* (seen in うかうか 'absentmindedly', originally linked to 浮く *uku* 'to float, be ungrounded'), describing a momentary lapse of attention ('absentmindedly, carelessly').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — うっかり

うなずく.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *unaduku* (頷く / 首づく), a compound of Old Japanese *una* (うな 'nape of the neck') + *tuku* (つく / 突く 'to thrust, dip downward'), literally 'to dip the neck in assent'.

history.meaning: dip the neck; nod in agreement

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頷く

うるさい.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *urusasi* (うるさし), which originally meant 'tedious, bothersome, overly complicated' or conversely 'skillful, thorough'. Often connected with Old Japanese *uraci / urasa* ('mental闷/constraint'). In Modern Japanese it means 'noisy, loud, fussy, annoying'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 煩い

え.etymology: Short native Japanese interjection of questioning, surprise, or request for repetition ('eh?, huh?'), attested across historical stages of spoken Japanese.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — え

ええ.etymology: Lengthened form of the interjection え. Depending on intonation, it serves either as a polite conversational affirmative ('yes, indeed', common from the late Edo/Meiji period) or an exclamation of surprise ('eh?!').

history.meaning: exclamation of emotion or affirmative response

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ええ

ええっ.etymology: Emphatic glottalized form of ええ with a final glottal stop (っ), expressing strong astonishment or disbelief ('what?! no way!').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ええ

えっ.etymology: Sharp glottalized interjection built on え ('eh?') with a final glottal stop, expressing sudden surprise or a taken-aback reaction ('huh?, wait, what?').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — えっ

えと.etymology: Conversational filler (also lengthened as ええと) used while searching for words or recalling information ('let me see, um'). Formed in Early Modern / Modern spoken Japanese from hesitation vowel え + quotative/linking particle と.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ええと

お.etymology: Honorific and beautifying prefix 御 (お-), which developed in Middle Japanese via phonetic reduction of earlier *oomi-* (大御 'great august') > *on-* (おん) > *o-* (お), primarily attached to native Japanese (*wago*) nouns, adjectives, and verb stems.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 御

おいしい.etymology: Originally a 15th-century court ladies' word (*nyōbō kotoba*) おいし ('delicious'), formed by attaching the honorific prefix お- to the Old/Middle Japanese adjective いし (美し 'pleasant, admirable, fine, sweet'). It gradually replaced うまい as the polite standard word for 'tasty, delicious'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 美味しい
Wiktionary — おいしい (美味しい) (Japanese)

おいで.etymology: Honorific noun and verbal expression 御出で (おいで), formed from polite prefix お- + 出で (continuative stem of 出づ / 出る 'to come out, go forth, appear'). Used in polite imperatives ('come here') and honorific constructions ('to come, go, or stay').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 御出で

おかけ.etymology: Honorific verbal noun 御掛け (おかけ), formed from polite prefix お- + かけ (continuative stem of かける 掛ける 'to hang, sit down upon a chair, pour, spend'). Frequently used in hospitality phrases such as おかけください ('please take a seat').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 掛ける

おかげ.etymology: Formed from honorific prefix お- (御) + かげ (陰 / 影 'shade, shelter, unseen divine protection'). Originally denoting the protective shelter of deities, Buddhas, or social superiors, it broadened into 'thanks to, owing to someone's help'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 御陰

おきて.etymology: Verbal noun 掟 (おきて 'rule, law, code'), nominalized from the continuative stem of the Old/Middle Japanese verb おきつ (掟つ 'to determine in advance, lay down, arrange', related to 置く *oku* 'to place, set').

history.form: おきつ (掟つ) → おきて

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 掟

おく.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *oku* (置く 'to put, place, leave as is, let settle'). After the *-te* form of another verb (〜ておく), it functions as an aspectual auxiliary indicating preparatory action or leaving something in a resulting state.

history.meaning: put down; set in place; leave behind
put; place; do in advance (~ておく)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 置く

おしゃべり.etymology: Polite/colloquial noun formed from prefix お- + しゃべり (nominalized stem of しゃべる 喋る 'to chat, chatter, talk', which emerged in Early Modern Japanese, likely from sound-symbolic *shaber-* 'wag the tongue').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お喋り

おじ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *wodi* (伯父・叔父 'uncle'), a reduced compound of 小 (を *wo* 'small, junior, secondary') + 父 (*ti* 'father, elder male kinsman', cf. ちち), contrasting with おほぢ (*ohodi* 'grandfather, great-father').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 伯父

おじいさん.etymology: Polite kinship and address term for 'grandfather' or an elderly man, formed from honorific prefix お- + じい (爺, from Old Japanese おほぢ *ohodi* 'grandfather', literally 'great-father') + polite suffix -さん.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お祖父さん

おじいちゃん.etymology: Affectionate familial form of おじいさん ('grandpa'), replacing polite -さん with the endearing diminutive suffix -ちゃん.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — おじいちゃん

おそろい.etymology: Polite nominalization formed from prefix お- + そろい (揃い, stem of そろう 揃う 'to become complete, match, be uniform'), denoting matching outfits, a matching set, or going together.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お揃い

おっと.etymology: Exclamation used when catching oneself after a near-slip or sudden realization ('whoops!, hold on!'), formed from the interjection お + glottal catch っ + particle と.

history.meaning: exclamation on suddenly stopping or catching a slip

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — おっと

おつり.etymology: Polite noun お釣り ('change returned after payment'), from prefix お- + つり (釣り 'balancing,吊り/釣り'). Originally from Edo-period money-changing where a difference in value between exchanged coins balanced the scales (*tsuri* 'equilibrium, counterbalance').

history.meaning: monetary balance returned in coin exchange

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お釣り

おでこ.etymology: Colloquial noun for the forehead ('brow'), formed from prefix お- + でこ (凸 'projection, prominence, bulging brow', related to でこぼこ 'uneven, bumpy').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — おでこ

おはよう.etymology: Morning greeting clipped from おはようございます ('good morning'), where はよう is the *u*-onbin euphonic adverbial form of はやい (早い 'early'), originally a backstage/household greeting acknowledging that someone has arrived or started work early.

history.meaning: you are early today -> good morning

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お早う

おはようございます.etymology: Polite morning greeting formed from honorific prefix お + the western/polite *-u* adverbial sound change (ウ音便) of 早い (*hayaku* > *hayō*, 'early') + polite verb ございます: literally 'It is early!'

sources.title: Wiktionary — おはようございます (Japanese)

おば.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *woba* (伯母・叔母 'aunt'), a reduced compound of 小 (を *wo* 'small, secondary, junior') + 母 (*ba / fa* 'mother, female elder', cf. はは), parallel to おじ ('uncle') and おば/おおば ('grandmother').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 伯母

おばさん.etymology: Polite kinship and address term for 'aunt' or a middle-aged woman, formed from polite prefix お- + ば (from おば 'aunt') + polite title suffix -さん.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 叔母さん

おもてなし.etymology: Polite verbal noun formed from prefix お- + もてなし (持て成し, nominalized stem of もてなす 'to treat, entertain, receive guests warmly', from 持つ *motu* 'hold, handle' + なす *nasu* 'accomplish, perform'). Also popularly associated by folk/secondary wordplay with 表なし ('without a false front, wholehearted').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — おもてなし

おや.etymology: Exclamation of mild surprise or curiosity ('oh?, hullo?, my!'), widely used from Edo-period colloquial Japanese onward; often thought to have arisen from calling out to one's parent (親 *oya*) in surprise.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — おや

おやすみなさい.etymology: Polite bedtime parting greeting ('good night') and polite imperative ('please rest'), formed from おやすみ (honorific prefix お- + 休み 'resting', stem of 休む *yasumu*) + polite imperative auxiliary なさい (from なさる).

history.form: おやすみなさりませ / おやすみなさい

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お休みなさい

お二人.etymology: Polite numeral-noun compound formed from honorific prefix お- + 二人 (ふたり 'two people', inherited from Old Japanese *putari*, from *puta-* 'two' + *-ri* human counter suffix).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お二人

お互い.etymology: Polite noun formed from prefix お- + 互い (たがい 'mutuality, each other'), nominalized from the Old/Middle Japanese verb たがふ (違ふ 'to cross, alternate, differ from one another').

history.meaning: each other; mutual; both of us

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お互い

お仕事.etymology: Polite form of 仕事 (しごと 'work, occupation'), which combines 仕 (し, stem of する 'to do', written with ateji 仕 'serve') + 事 (ごと, voiced from こと 'matter, thing, task').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お仕事

お会計.etymology: Polite hospitality and retail term formed from prefix お- + Sino-Japanese 会計 (かいけい 'accounting, bill, settlement', from 会 'gather, total' + 計 'calculate, reckon').

history.meaning: the bill; check; payment at a register

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お会計

お似合い.etymology: Polite nominalization formed from prefix お- + 似合い (にあい, stem of 似合う 'to suit each other, be well-matched', a compound of 似る *niru* 'resemble, be fitting' + 合う *au* 'match, come together').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お似合い

お兄さん.etymology: Polite kinship and address term for 'older brother' or a young man, formed from honorific prefix お- + 兄 (にい, evolved via vowel lengthening from Old Japanese あに *ani* 'elder brother') + polite suffix -さん.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お兄さん
Wiktionary — おにいさん (お兄さん) (Japanese)

お兄ちゃん.etymology: Affectionate familial address and reference term for an older brother ('big brother'), formed from お兄さん by replacing -さん with the endearing diminutive suffix -ちゃん.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お兄ちゃん

お前.etymology: Originally an honorific noun 御前 (おまえ 'before a deity, noble, or high personage'), from prefix お- (御) + 前 (まえ 'front, presence'). Through centuries of indirect reference to the person sitting in front of the speaker, its social register bleached in late Edo and Modern Japanese into an informal or rough second-person pronoun ('you').

history.meaning: the honorable presence of a noble or deity

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お前

お名前.etymology: Polite noun for 'name', formed from honorific prefix お- + 名前 (なまえ, originally a compound of 名 *na* 'name' + 前 *mae* 'portion/standing, front', attested from the Edo period as a fuller synonym of 名).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お名前

お嬢.etymology: Polite/familiar form combining prefix お- with Sino-Japanese 嬢 (じょう 'young lady, unmarried daughter'), also used as a clipping of お嬢さん / お嬢様 ('young lady, miss').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お嬢

お客さま.etymology: High-respect hospitality term ('honored guest, customer'), formed from honorific prefix お- + Sino-Japanese 客 (きゃく 'guest, visitor, customer') + honorific suffix -さま (様).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お客様

お客さん.etymology: Everyday polite term for 'guest, visitor, customer', formed from prefix お- + Sino-Japanese 客 (きゃく 'guest') + polite suffix -さん (derived from -さま).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お客さん

お店.etymology: Polite everyday noun for 'shop, store, restaurant', formed from prefix お- + 店 (みせ, nominalized stem of 見せる *miseru* 'to show, display wares on a shelf').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お店

お昼.etymology: Polite everyday noun for 'noon, midday' or 'lunch', formed from prefix お- + 昼 (ひる 'daytime, noon', inherited from Old Japanese *piru*). The lunch sense arose from court ladies' speech (*nyōbō kotoba*) shortening お昼飯.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お昼

お気.etymology: Polite noun formed from honorific prefix お- + Sino-Japanese 気 (き 'spirit, mind, attention, care'), used in set polite expressions such as お気をつけて ('please take care') and お気に召す ('to please one's fancy').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お気

お気に入り.etymology: Polite compound noun ('favorite'), nominalized from the phrase お気に入る ('to enter into someone's favor/liking'), combining お気 ('one's mind/fancy') + particle に + 入り (stem of 入る *iru* 'to enter').

history.meaning: one who pleases a master; favorite

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お気に入り

お水.etymology: Polite everyday word for '(cold/drinking) water', formed from beautifying prefix お- + 水 (みず, inherited from Old Japanese *midu* 'water'). Originating in court ladies' speech (*nyōbō kotoba* おひや / おみず), it is now universal in dining and hospitality.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お水

お湯.etymology: Polite everyday word for 'hot water' or 'warm bath', formed from beautifying prefix お- + 湯 (ゆ 'hot water, hot spring, bath', inherited from Old Japanese *yu*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お湯

お知らせ.etymology: Polite verbal noun ('notice, announcement, notification'), formed from prefix お- + 知らせ (nominalized stem of 知らせる 'to let know, inform', causative of 知る *siru* 'to know').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お知らせ

お知り合い.etymology: Polite compound noun ('acquaintance'), formed from prefix お- + 知り合い (nominalized stem of 知り合う 'to know one another', from 知る 'know' + reciprocal 合う 'do mutually').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お知り合い

お礼.etymology: Polite hybrid formation combining prefix お- with Sino-Japanese 礼 (れい 'propriety, bow, ceremony, gratitude'). From 'a ceremonial bow of respect', it specialized in everyday Japanese for 'thanks, expression of gratitude, return gift'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お礼

お腹.etymology: Polite everyday word for 'stomach, belly', originating in Muromachi court ladies' speech (*nyōbō kotoba*) おなか, which attached prefix お- to 中 (なか 'middle, inside of the body') as a refined avoidance term for 腹 (はら 'belly'). Written with the kanji お腹 via semantic matching (*jukujikun*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お腹

お茶.etymology: Polite everyday word for 'tea' (especially Japanese green tea), formed from beautifying prefix お- + Sino-Japanese 茶 (ちゃ 'tea', borrowed from Middle Chinese *drae*). Used both for the beverage and for taking a break over tea.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お茶

お茶会.etymology: Polite compound noun ('tea gathering, tea party'), formed from お茶 ('tea') + Sino-Japanese 会 (かい 'gathering, meeting').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お茶会

お言葉.etymology: Polite noun ('your words, kind offer, remark'), formed from honorific prefix お- + 言葉 (ことば 'word, speech, language', from Old Japanese *kotoba*, compounding 言 *koto* 'speech, word' + 端/葉 *pa* 'edge, leaf, manifestation').

history.meaning: someone's respected words or kind offer

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お言葉

お詫び.etymology: Polite verbal noun ('apology'), formed from prefix お- + 詫び (わび, nominalized stem of 詫びる 'to apologize; feel distressed or penitent', continuing Old Japanese *wabu* 'to languish, be at a loss, feel remorse').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お詫び

お迎え.etymology: Polite verbal noun ('meeting, welcoming, picking someone up'), formed from prefix お- + 迎え (むかえ, nominalized stem of 迎える 'to go out to meet, welcome', from Old Japanese *mukapu* 'to face toward', derived from 向く *muku*).

history.meaning: going to meet or pick someone up (polite)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お迎え

お過ごし.etymology: Honorific verbal stem 御過ごし (おすごし), formed from prefix お- + 過ごし (stem of 過ごす 'to pass time, spend one's days', transitive counterpart of 過ぐ *sugu* 'to pass by'). Used in polite seasonal and well-wishing formulas.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 過ごす

お邪魔.etymology: Polite expression ('intrusion, visiting someone's home'), formed from prefix お- + Sino-Japanese Buddhist term 邪魔 (じゃま 'evil Mara demon hindering enlightenment' -> 'hindrance, obstacle, intrusion'). Used in greetings like お邪魔します ('excuse my intrusion').

history.meaning: intrusion; visiting another's home or room

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お邪魔

お部屋.etymology: Polite everyday noun for 'room', formed from beautifying prefix お- + 部屋 (へや, originally 隔屋 *he-ya* 'partitioned-off chamber or outbuilding', from 隔 *he* 'partition, interval' + 屋 *ya* 'building, room').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お部屋

お酢.etymology: Polite culinary noun for 'vinegar', formed from beautifying prefix お- + 酢 (す 'vinegar', inherited from Old Japanese *su*, cognate with the adjective 酸い *sui* 'sour').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お酢

お金.etymology: Polite and standard everyday word for 'money', formed from beautifying prefix お- + 金 (かね 'metal, gold/silver, coin', inherited from Old Japanese *kane*). Originating in refined speech, お金 became the default conversational noun for money.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お金

お隣さん.etymology: Friendly polite noun for 'next-door neighbor', formed from prefix お- + 隣 (となり 'next door, adjacent house', from Old Japanese *tonari*, related to 連なる 'stand in a row') + polite suffix -さん.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お隣

お電話.etymology: Polite noun ('telephone, phone call'), formed from prefix お- + Meiji-era Sino-Japanese coinage 電話 (でんわ 'telephone', from 電 'electricity, lightning' + 話 'speech, talk').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お電話

お願い.etymology: Polite verbal noun ('request, wish, favor, prayer'), formed from prefix お- + 願い (ねがい, nominalized stem of 願う 'to pray for, wish, request', inherited from Old Japanese *negapu*, an iterative of *negu* 'to pray, soothe a deity's spirit').

history.form: ねがふ (願ふ) → ねがひ

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お願い

お風呂.etymology: Polite everyday word for 'bath, bathtub, bathroom', formed from beautifying prefix お- + 風呂 (ふろ, originally a steam bath or sweat lodge, related to 室 *muro* 'enclosed cellar/steam chamber').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — お風呂

か.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ka*, a *kakari-joshi* (focus particle) expressing doubt, questioning, or alternatives. When *kakari-musubi* declined in Late Middle Japanese, sentence-final か became the universal question-marking particle.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — か

かかと.etymology: Inherited from earlier Japanese *kakato* (踵 'heel of the foot'), attested from late medieval/early modern lexicons as a shift or compound alongside older Old Japanese *kubisu / kibisu* ('heel'); often analyzed as 掛処 (*kaka-to* 'place where weight/sandal-cord catches').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 踵

かかる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kakaru* (掛かる・懸かる・罹る), the intransitive counterpart of かける (*kaku* 'to hang, attach, apply'). From 'to hang upon, catch on', it developed wide senses including 'take time/money', 'start working', and 'fall ill'.

history.form: かかる (掛かる・懸かる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 掛かる

かぐ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kagu* (嗅ぐ 'to smell, sniff, scent'), cognate with Old Japanese *ka* (香 'scent, aroma, fragrance').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 嗅ぐ

かける.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) verb 掛ける・懸ける, continuing Old Japanese *kaku* ('to hang, suspend, hook onto'), transitive counterpart of かかる. Expanded to numerous idiomatic senses: 'put on (glasses)', 'pour over', 'make a phone call', 'spend time', and 'sit down'.

history.meaning: hang; put on; pour; call; spend (time)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 掛ける

かご.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kago / ko* (籠 'woven bamboo basket or cage'), attested in eighth-century texts. Likely a compound containing old *ko* ('basket') and *kago* ('enclosure').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 籠

かしら.etymology: Sentence-final particle expressing gentle self-directed wondering ('I wonder if...'), contracted in Early Modern Japanese from か知らん (*ka shiran*), itself from question particle か + 知らぬ ('I do not know [whether]...').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — かしら

かな.etymology: Compound sentence-final particle formed in Early Modern and Modern Japanese from the question particle か + the reflective/emotive particle な ('I wonder, could it be'), distinct in function from the classical poetic exclamation かな (哉).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — かな

かも.etymology: Colloquial epistemic particle ('might, maybe, perhaps') clipped from かもしれない ('cannot be known whether -> might be'), preserving the question particle か and inclusive particle も.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — かも

から.etymology: Case and conjunctive particle with older spatial and temporal uses marking a starting point or route ('from'). Its causal clause use ('because, since') developed in Early Modern Japanese, with dictionary citations from around 1710.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — から

からから.etymology: Reduplicated onomatopoeic and mimetic adverb representing a dry rattling or clattering sound, and by extension a completely parched, bone-dry state ('parched, dry as a bone, rattling').

history.meaning: sound of dry objects clattering or hearty laughter

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — からから

かわいい.etymology: Evolved from Early Middle Japanese *kapayusi* (かはゆし 'flushed-faced, embarrassed, pitiable, touching', a compound of 顔 *kapa* 'face' + 映ゆし *payusi* 'glowing, tingling'). From feeling tender pity for someone vulnerable ('touching, dear'), it shifted in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese to 'darling, adorable, cute'.

history.form: かはいらしい / かはゆい

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 可愛い

が.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ga*, originally a possessive/genitive particle (as preserved in 我が家 *wa ga ie* 'my home') linking animate nouns to possessed nouns or nominalized clauses. In Late Middle Japanese, subjects of subordinate clauses marked by が reanalyzed into main-clause nominative subjects ('subject marker が') and clause-linking 'but'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — が

がたつき.etymology: Verbal noun derived from the continuative stem of がたつく ('to rattle, wobble, be loose'), itself built on the onomatopoeic root がた- (from がたがた 'rattling, shaking') + verbalizing suffix -つく.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — がたつく

きっと.etymology: Mimetic and modal adverb attested from Late Heian and Kamakura tales as きと / きっと, originally describing a sharp, tense, or decisive action ('tightly, sternly, without fail'). In Modern Japanese its epistemic sense 'surely, undoubtedly' predominates.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 屹度

きれい.etymology: Sino-Japanese adjectival noun 綺麗 (きれい), borrowed from Middle Chinese *khjeX lejH* (綺麗 'fine patterned silk; splendid and graceful'). In Japanese it broadened from 'splendid, beautiful' to include 'clean, neat, tidy, pure'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 綺麗

くせ.etymology: Inherited from Old/Early Middle Japanese *kuse* (癖 'habit, peculiarity, crease, flaw in posture or behavior'). Also used grammatically in 〜くせに ('despite, even though') from 'with the peculiarity of'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 癖

ください.etymology: Polite request form ('please give me; please do'), arisen in Early Modern Japanese by phonological reduction of くだされ (*kudasare*, imperative of the honorific verb くださる 下さる 'to bestow from above').

history.meaning: please give me; please do (~てください)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 下さい

くださる.etymology: Honorific verb 下さる ('for a respected person to give'), evolved in Late Middle Japanese from 下さる (*kudasaru*, originally the passive/honorific form of 下す *kudasu* 'to hand down from above, bestow').

history.meaning: be handed down from a superior; deign to bestow

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 下さる

くらい.etymology: Inherited from Old/Early Middle Japanese *kurawi* (位 'court rank, station, seat'), literally 'the place where one sits' (座 *kura* 'seat, platform' + 居 *wi* 'sitting'). From 'rank, grade, level', it grammaticalized into a particle indicating approximate degree ('about, approximately, to the extent of').

history.meaning: seat of rank; social station; grade

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 位
Wiktionary — くらい / ぐらい (Japanese)

くるみ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kurumi* (胡桃 'walnut'), attested in tenth-century lexicons such as the *Wamyō Ruijushō*; often analyzed as combining *kuro-* ('dark') + *mi* ('nut, fruit') from the dark stain of walnut husks.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 胡桃

くれる.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) verb 呉れる, continuing Old Japanese *kuru* ('to give to the speaker or an inferior'). Also used after a *-te* verb (〜てくれる) as the benefactive auxiliary indicating someone does a favor for the speaker.

history.meaning: give (to me/in-group); do as a favor

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 呉れる

くん.etymology: Familiar honorific title suffix 君 (-くん), using the Sino-Japanese *on'yomi* of 君 ('lord, prince, gentleman'). Popularized among late Edo and Meiji students and officials as a camaraderie address term, and now used for boys, male peers, or juniors.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 君

ぐっすり.etymology: Mimetic adverb attested from the Edo period onward, built on the voiced sound-symbolic root *gusu-* + intensive gemination and *-ri* suffix, describing deep, sound, undisturbed sleep ('soundly, fast asleep').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ぐっすり

けど.etymology: Colloquial conjunctive particle ('but, although, however'), formed in Early Modern Japanese by shortening けれど (itself from the concessive inflection *-keredo* of the classical past/retrospective auxiliary けり).

history.meaning: although it is the case that

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — けど

けやき通り.etymology: Compound street name ('Keyaki Avenue / Zelkova Street'), combining けやき (欅 'Japanese zelkova tree', *Zelkova serrata*, related to けやけし 'conspicuous, striking' for its stately grain and canopy) + 通り (とおり 'street, avenue', stem of 通る 'to pass through').

history.form: けやき (欅) + 通り (とおり)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 欅

けれど.etymology: Conjunctive particle and conjunction ('however, although'), grammaticalized in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese by detaching the concessive form (*izenkei* けれ + concessive particle ど) of classical adjectival and auxiliary inflections.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — けれど

こうして.etymology: Conjunctive phrase ('thus, in this way'), formed from the proximal manner adverb こう (from classical かく *kaku* 'thus' via *kau* > *kō*) + して (the *-te* form of する 'to do').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 斯うして

ここ.etymology: Proximal spatial demonstrative pronoun ('here, this place'), inherited from Old Japanese *koko* (此処), formed by reduplicating the proximal deictic root こ- ('this') or combining こ- + locative element *-ko* ('place').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 此処

こちら.etymology: Polite proximal directional and personal demonstrative ('this way, this side, this person, I/we'), formed from the proximal root こ- ('this') + directional suffix -ちら (which developed in Middle Japanese from earlier -ち + plural/locative -ら).

history.meaning: this way; this one; this person (polite)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 此方

こっち.etymology: Colloquial proximal directional demonstrative ('this way, this side, over here'), evolved in Middle/Early Modern Japanese via consonant gemination from Old Japanese こち (*koti* 'this direction, hither', from こ- 'this' + directional suffix *-ti*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 此方

こと.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *koto* (事 'intangible matter, affair, event, fact' and 言 'word, speech', originally a single root meaning 'what is spoken of / an event or state of affairs'). In grammar it also functions as an abstract clause nominalizer.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 事

こねる.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) verb 捏ねる, continuing Early Middle Japanese *konu* ('to knead, mix clay or dough with water and work with the hands'), cognate with こなす ('to work down, digest, handle skillfully').

history.meaning: knead clay or dough; mix thoroughly
knead (dough, clay); work with the hands

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 捏ねる

この.etymology: Proximal adnominal demonstrative ('this'), inherited from Old Japanese *kono* (此の), composed of the proximal deictic root こ ('this') + attributive/genitive particle の.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 此の

こぼす.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *kobosu* (零す・溢す 'to spill, shed tears, grumble'), the transitive counterpart of こぼれる ('to spill over, overflow').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 零す

こぼれる.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) verb 零れる・溢れる, continuing Early Middle Japanese *koboru* ('to overflow, spill out, fall in drops, chip at the edge'), intransitive counterpart of こぼす.

history.meaning: spill over; fall in drops; overflow

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 零れる

これ.etymology: Proximal demonstrative pronoun ('this, this one'), inherited from Old Japanese *kore* (此・之), built from the proximal deictic root こ ('this') + pronominal suffix -れ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 此れ

こんな.etymology: Adnominal demonstrative ('this kind of, such a'), formed in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese by phonetic contraction of このような (*kono yō na* 'of this manner') > こやうな > こんな.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — こんな

こんなに.etymology: Adverbial form of こんな ('like this, to this extent, so much'), formed by attaching the adverbial particle に to the contracted stem こんな- (from このように).

history.meaning: in such a way; to this extent

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — こんなに

こんにちは.etymology: Standard daytime greeting ('hello, good afternoon'), shortened from conversational openings such as 今日はご機嫌いかがですか ('How are your spirits today?'), where 今日 (こんにち 'today') is marked by the topic particle は (still spelled with は).

history.meaning: 'As for today, [it is fine weather / how are you]...'

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 今日は

こんばんは.etymology: Standard evening greeting ('good evening'), shortened from conversational openings such as 今晩は良い晩ですね ('Tonight is a fine evening, isn't it?'), combining 今晩 (こんばん 'this evening') + topic particle は.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 今晩は

ご.etymology: Honorific and polite prefix 御 (ご-), using the Sino-Japanese *go-on* reading of 御 ('imperial, august, honorable'). Primarily prefixed to Sino-Japanese (*kango*) nouns and verbal nouns, complementary to native お-.

history.meaning: polite and honorific prefix for Sino-Japanese words

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 御

ございます.etymology: Polite existential and copular verb ('to be, exist'), formed by attaching the polite auxiliary ます to ござる (御座る, which contracted in Late Middle Japanese from 御座ある *goza aru* 'to have an honorable seat -> honorifically exist').

history.form: ござある (御座ある) → ござる
history.meaning: exist honorifically (lit. have an honorable seat)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 御座います

ごちそう.etymology: Formed from honorific prefix ご- (御) + Sino-Japanese 馳走 (ちそう 'running about on horseback'). Originally referring to a host riding and bustling about to gather fresh ingredients for a guest, it came to mean 'a lavish feast, hospitality, treat'.

history.meaning: galloping and running about; bustling in service

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 御馳走

ごと.etymology: Suffix 毎 (-ごと 'every, each; whole, including'), inherited from Old Japanese *goto* (as in 日ごと 'every day'), cognate with 如し (*gotosi* 'like, similar to', from the notion of things following the same pattern one after another).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 毎

ごみ箱.etymology: Compound noun ('trash can, wastebasket'), combining ごみ (塵・芥 'dust, litter, rubbish', originally pine needles or sediment settling in water, related to 込む *komu*) + 箱 (はこ > ばこ via rendaku, 'box, bin', from Old Japanese *pako*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塵箱

ごらん.etymology: Honorific noun and polite imperative 御覧 (ごらん 'looking, seeing; please look'), formed from honorific prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 覧 (らん 'to view, inspect'). Used standalone ('look') or in ご覧になる / ご覧ください.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 御覧

ご一緒.etymology: Polite noun and verbal noun ('together, accompanying someone'), formed from honorific prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 一緒 (いっしょ 'together, same place', originally Buddhist/medieval 一処 'one place', later written 一緒 'one thread/lineage').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ご一緒

ご兄弟.etymology: Polite kinship noun ('brothers and sisters, siblings'), formed from honorific prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 兄弟 (きょうだい, from 兄 'elder brother' + 弟 'younger brother', broadened to siblings in general).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ご兄弟

ご夫婦.etymology: Polite noun ('married couple, husband and wife'), formed from honorific prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 夫婦 (ふうふ, from 夫 'husband' + 婦 'wife').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ご夫婦

ご存じ.etymology: Honorific noun ('knowing, being aware'), formed from prefix ご- + 存じ (continuative stem of the hybrid Sino-Japanese verb 存ずる / 存じる 'to think, know, keep in mind', from Sino-Japanese 存 *zon* 'exist, hold in mind' + する).

history.form: ごぞんじ (御存知・御存じ)

history.meaning: knowing (honorific, in ご存じですか / ご存じの通り)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 御存じ

ご安心.etymology: Polite verbal noun ('peace of mind, relief'), formed from prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 安心 (あんしん, originally a Buddhist term meaning 'resting the mind in faith', from 安 'peaceful, calm' + 心 'heart, mind').

history.form: 安心 (あんじん / あんしん)
history.meaning: calming the heart; peace of mind
relief; peace of mind (polite, e.g. ご安心ください)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 安心

ご家族.etymology: Polite noun ('someone's family'), formed from honorific prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 家族 (かぞく 'family, household members', from 家 'house, home' + 族 'clan, kin').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ご家族

ご案内.etymology: Polite noun and verbal noun ('guidance, showing around, announcement'), formed from prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 案内 (あんない, from 案 'desk, document, plan' + 内 'inside contents', which evolved in Heian Japanese from 'contents of a document' to 'prior knowledge of a place' and 'guiding someone').

history.meaning: contents of a matter; inside familiarity; guidance

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ご案内

ご用意.etymology: Polite noun and verbal noun ('preparation, readiness'), formed from prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 用意 (ようい, from 用 'use, employ' + 意 'mind, attention', shifting from 'mental attentiveness' to 'preparing in advance').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ご用意

ご自分.etymology: Polite reflexive pronoun ('yourself, oneself'), formed from honorific prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 自分 (じぶん 'oneself', from 自 'self' + 分 'portion, status').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ご自分

ご親切.etymology: Polite adjectival noun ('kindness, goodwill'), formed from prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 親切 (しんせつ, from 親 'intimate, close' + 切 'earnest, keen,切実', originally meaning 'keenly close and earnest').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 親切

ご近所.etymology: Polite noun ('neighborhood, neighbors'), formed from prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 近所 (きんじょ 'nearby place, neighborhood', from 近 'near' + 所 'place').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ご近所

ご迷惑.etymology: Polite noun ('trouble, inconvenience, annoyance'), formed from prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 迷惑 (めいわく, originally a Buddhist/Chinese compound of 迷 'go astray' + 惑 'be bewildered', which shifted in Early Modern Japanese to 'being troubled or inconvenienced by someone').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ご迷惑

ご選択.etymology: Polite verbal noun ('selection, choice'), formed from prefix ご- + Sino-Japanese 選択 (せんたく, from 選 'choose, select' + 択 'pick out').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 選択

さ.etymology: Colloquial sentence-final and interjectional particle ('you know, of course, well') that emerged in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese, generally derived from the distal/anaphoric demonstrative adverb さ (然 'so, like that', asserting 'that is how it is').

history.meaning: sentence-final particle of light assertion; filler particle

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — さ

さあ.etymology: Native Japanese interjection used either to prompt action ('come on!, well now, here we go') or to express hesitant uncertainty ('well..., I'm not sure'), formed by lengthening the deictic/exclamatory syllable さ.

history.meaning: interjection urging action or expressing hesitation

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — さあ

さえ.etymology: Focus particle inherited from Old Japanese *sape* (さへ, spelled さへ in historical kana). Originally meaning 'in addition, furthermore' (linked to 添ふ *sopu* 'to add to, accompany'), in Late Middle and Modern Japanese it absorbed the extreme-example function of classical だに ('even').

history.meaning: in addition; on top of that

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — さえ

さっき.etymology: Temporal noun and adverb ('a little while ago, just now'), arisen by consonant gemination from さき (先 'earlier, before, a moment ago', inherited from Old Japanese *saki*).

history.meaning: a short while ago; just now

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — さっき

さっと.etymology: Mimetic adverb with gemination and quotative/adverbial particle と on a sibilant root *sa-* (attested in Heian/Kamakura texts as さと / さっと), evoking a swift, light, brisk movement, gust, or glance ('quickly, briskly, in a flash').

history.meaning: suddenly; swiftly; with a light rush

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — さっと

さま.etymology: Inherited from Old/Early Middle Japanese *sama* (様 'manner, state, appearance, direction'). From respectful indirect reference to 'the direction or manner of a high personage', it grammaticalized in Late Middle Japanese into the polite honorific title suffix -さま (様).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 様

さようなら.etymology: Standard parting greeting ('goodbye, farewell'), shortened in Early Modern Japanese from the conditional transition phrase 左様ならば (*sayō naraba* 'if that is so, that being the case, [I shall take my leave]').

history.form: さやうならば (左様ならば)
history.meaning: if it be so; in that case

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 左様なら

さわる.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *sawaru* (触る 'to touch, come into contact with'), originally overlapping with 障る (*sawaru* 'to bump into, hinder, affect'). In Modern Japanese 触る denotes physical touching or feeling with the hand.

history.meaning: come into contact with; brush against

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 触る

さん.etymology: Standard polite title suffix (-さん 'Mr., Ms.') that arose in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese via phonological wear and nasalization of the honorific suffix -さま (様 *sama* > *san*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — さん

ざっと.etymology: Mimetic and manner adverb with voiced initial *za-* (contrasting with lighter さっと), attested from Late Middle Japanese for the rushing sound of water/wind and by extension doing something roughly, briskly, or in broad strokes ('roughly, briefly, approximately').

history.meaning: with a rush; roughly; in brief

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ざっと

し.etymology: Conjunctive particle ('and, what's more, besides') listing non-exhaustive reasons or qualities. Evolved from the classical continuative/conclusive inflection *-si* (originally the past/perfective auxiliary き's attributive form or adjective stem), grammaticalized as a clause linker by Late Middle Japanese.

history.meaning: and besides; not only... but also

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — し

しか.etymology: Restrictive focus particle used with a negative predicate ('only, nothing but'), evolved in Early Modern Japanese from the comparative particle し (emphatic) + か (question/focus), or from しか ('thus, to that extent', cf. しかじ 'nothing is better than').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — しか

しかも.etymology: Conjunctive adverb ('moreover, furthermore, and yet'), formed in Old and Early Middle Japanese from the anaphoric adverb しか (然 'so, thus') + inclusive/concessive particle も ('even, also'), literally 'even while being so'.

history.meaning: moreover; what is more; and yet

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 然も

しっかり.etymology: Mimetic adverb formed on the root *shika-* (seen in しかと 'firmly, certainly', attested since Early Middle Japanese) with consonant gemination and the adverbial suffix *-ri*, meaning 'firmly, tightly, reliably, steadily'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — しっかり

しまう.etymology: Inherited from Late Middle / Early Modern Japanese 仕舞う・終う (*simapu* 'to bring to an end, finish, put away'), originally derived from 仕舞 (*simai* 'performing a dance / finishing a task'). After a *-te* verb (〜てしまう), it functions as an aspectual auxiliary of completion or regrettable outcome.

history.meaning: finish; put away; end up doing (~てしまう)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 仕舞う

しょっぱい.etymology: Eastern and standard colloquial adjective ('salty'), contracted in Early Modern Japanese from 塩っぱい (*shioppai*), a compound of 塩 (しお 'salt') + adjectival suffix -っぱい ('full of the taste/quality of', from 一杯 *ippai*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塩っぱい

しれる.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) verb 知れる, continuing Early Middle Japanese *siru* ('to become known, come to light'), the spontaneous/potential counterpart of 知る ('to know'). Preserved in modern expressions like かもしれない ('might be').

history.meaning: become known; be possible to know

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 知れる

じっと.etymology: Mimetic adverb attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese, describing unmoving concentration, stillness, or patient endurance ('motionlessly, fixedly, patiently').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — じっと

じゃあ.etymology: Colloquial conjunction and discourse transition marker ('well then, in that case, if so'), contracted in Edo-period eastern Japanese from では (*de wa* > *jaa*), itself composed of copular/locative で + topic particle は.

history.meaning: well then; if so; bye then

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — じゃあ

じゃあね.etymology: Casual parting greeting ('see you, bye then'), formed from the conversational transition marker じゃあ ('well then') + sentence-final rapport particle ね.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — じゃあ

じゅう.etymology: Sino-Japanese suffix 中 (-じゅう 'throughout, all over, during the entire'), voiced via rendaku from ちゅう (Middle Chinese *trjuwng* 'middle, inside, throughout'). Also represents the Sino-Japanese numeral 十 (じゅう 'ten').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 中

じろじろ.etymology: Reduplicated mimetic adverb attested from Early Modern Japanese, describing the action of staring intently, rudely, or inquisitively at someone or something.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — じろじろ

す.etymology: Classical conclusive form of the verb する (為 'to do'), and short causative/honorific verbal suffix (-す) inherited from Old Japanese *-su*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — す

すぎる.etymology: Upper bigrade (now ichidan) verb 過ぎる, continuing Old Japanese *sugu* ('to pass by, pass through, elapse, exceed'). Attached to verb stems and adjective roots, it functions as the productive suffix meaning 'too much, excessively'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 過ぎる

すぐ.etymology: Inherited from Old/Early Middle Japanese stem *sugu* (直 'straight, direct, upright, without detour'). From spatial 'directly, straight ahead', it shifted in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese to temporal immediacy ('right away, immediately, soon').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 直ぐ

すごい.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *sugosi* (凄し 'chillingly desolate, eerie, dreadful, awe-inspiring'). In Early Modern and Modern Japanese, the sense broadened from 'dreadfully intense' to a general intensifier meaning 'amazing, terrific, tremendous'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 凄い

すっかり.etymology: Mimetic adverb attested from the Edo period, formed on a root *suka-* ('cleared out, empty, clean through') with gemination and *-ri* suffix, meaning 'completely, entirely, through and through'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — すっかり

すっきり.etymology: Mimetic adverb formed on the root *suki-* (linked to 透く *suku* 'to become clear, open up, leave no clutter') with gemination and *-ri* suffix, describing a refreshed, uncluttered, or clear-headed state ('refreshed, neat, cleanly').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — すっきり

すべて.etymology: Adverb and noun 全て・総て ('all, everything, entirely'), derived from the *te*-form (*subete*) of the Old/Classical Japanese verb すぶ (統ぶ・総ぶ 'to gather into one, unite, govern as a whole').

history.form: すぶ (統ぶ・総ぶ) → すべて
history.meaning: gathering together into one; in total

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 全て

すみません.etymology: Standard polite apology and expression of gratitude ('excuse me, I'm sorry, thank you for your trouble'), literally the polite negative form of 済む (*sumu* 'to be settled, finished, clear of obligation'): 'my obligation/feeling toward you is not settled'.

history.form: すみませぬ (済みませぬ)
history.meaning: it does not settle my debt/conscience

history.form: すみません (済みません)
history.meaning: excuse me; I am sorry; thank you

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 済みません
Wiktionary — すみません (済みません) (Japanese)

すりガラス.etymology: Hybrid compound noun 擦りガラス ('frosted glass, ground glass'), combining native 擦り (すり, stem of 擦る *suru* 'to rub, grind, frost by abrasion') + Dutch loanword ガラス (from Dutch *glas* 'glass').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 擦りガラス
Wiktionary — すりガラス (擦り硝子) (Japanese)

すり減る.etymology: Compound verb 擦り減る ('to wear down, be worn away by friction'), combining 擦り (すり, stem of 擦る *suru* 'to rub, chafe') + 減る (へる 'to decrease, diminish').

history.meaning: wear down by rubbing; be abraded

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 擦り減る
Wiktionary — すりへる (擦り減る) (Japanese)

する.etymology: Standard irregular verb 為る ('to do, make, perform'), continuing Old Japanese *su* (attributive *suru*). By Late Middle Japanese the attributive form する generalized to replace the classical conclusive form す.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 為る

ず.etymology: Classical and modern negative auxiliary/conjunctive suffix (-ず 'without doing, not'), inherited from Old Japanese *-zu*, which arose by fusion of the old negative infinitive *-ni* + existential verb *su* ('to do/be').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ず

ずいぶん.etymology: Sino-Japanese adverb and adjectival noun 随分 (ずいぶん), from 随 ('follow, accord with') + 分 ('one's lot, status, station'). Originally meaning 'in accordance with one's station', it shifted in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese to 'considerably, very, quite a lot'.

history.meaning: befitting one's status; to the best of one's ability
considerably; very; quite a long time

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 随分

ずっと.etymology: Mimetic and degree adverb attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese, describing continuous unbroken movement or duration ('straight through, all the time') or a large gap in comparison ('by far, much more').

history.meaning: all along; the whole time; much (more)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ずっと

ずつ.etymology: Distributive suffix/particle (-ずつ 'each, apiece, at a time'), inherited from Early Middle Japanese *dutu* (づつ, attached after numerals and quantities to indicate equal distribution or incremental steps).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 宛

ずぶ濡れ.etymology: Compound noun ずぶ濡れ ('soaked to the skin, sopping wet'), combining the mimetic root ずぶ (describing plunging completely into water, as in ずぶと / ずぶり) + 濡れ (ぬれ, nominalized stem of 濡れる 'to get wet').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ずぶ濡れ

ずり落ちる.etymology: Compound verb ずり落ちる ('to slip down, slide off'), combining ずり (stem of ずる 'to slide, drag along a surface') + 落ちる (おちる 'to fall, drop').

history.form: ずりおちる (ずり落ちる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ずり落ちる
Wiktionary — ずりおちる (ずり落ちる) (Japanese)

せい.etymology: Noun 所為 (せい 'fault, cause, due to'), evolved in Middle Japanese from せ (Sino-Japanese or native root linked to 為 'doing, action' or 勢 *sei* 'force, influence'), specializing in negative or unwelcome causes ('because of, someone's fault') in contrast to おかげ.

history.meaning: fault; blame; due to (an unwanted cause)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 所為

せめて.etymology: Adverb ('at least, if nothing else'), grammaticalized in Early Middle Japanese from the *te*-form of the verb せむ (迫む / 攻む 'to press hard, urge, push to the limit'): from 'pressing to the utmost', it came to express a minimum earnest wish.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — せめて

せる.etymology: Causative auxiliary suffix (-せる, attached to *godan* verbs), evolved in Late Middle Japanese when the lower bigrade classical causative suffix -す (attributive -する) shifted to ichidan conjugation (-せる).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — せる

せーの.etymology: Colloquial coordinating call ('one, two, three!; ready, heave!') used when lifting something or starting an action together. Commonly traced to せいの (from 勢 *sei* 'vigor, force' + の, or shortened from 一斉に *issei ni* / せえの).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — せえの
Wiktionary — せえの / せーの (Japanese)

ぜひ.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and adverb 是非 (ぜひ), from 是 ('right, this') + 非 ('wrong, not'). Originally a noun meaning 'right and wrong, pros and cons', in Late Middle Japanese phrases like 是非とも ('whether right or wrong, no matter what') it became an adverb meaning 'by all means, certainly'.

history.meaning: by all means; without fail; please

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 是非

そう.etymology: Mesial/anaphoric manner adverb ('so, in that way, yes') and evidential auxiliary ('looks like, I hear that'). Both derive via *u*-onbin (*sau* > *sō*) from Early Middle Japanese さう: the adverb from 然 (さ 'so, thus' + う), and the auxiliary from 様 (さま > さう 'appearance, manner').

history.meaning: so; like that; seems to be

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 然う

そういう.etymology: Adnominal phrase ('that kind of, such a'), composed of the manner adverb そう ('in that way, like that') + the verb いう (言う 'to say, call'), literally 'called like that'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — そう言う
Wiktionary — そういう (そう言う) (Japanese)

そこ.etymology: Mesial spatial demonstrative pronoun ('there, that place near you, that point just mentioned'), inherited from Old Japanese *soko* (其処), formed from the mesial deictic root そ- ('that') + locative suffix *-ko* ('place').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其処

そして.etymology: Conjunction ('and, and then'), formed from the anaphoric adverb そう (shortened to そ- in 然して *soshite* 'doing so') + して (the *-te* form of する 'to do').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 然して

そっくり.etymology: Mimetic and degree adverb attested from the Edo period, formed on a root *soku-* with gemination and *-ri* suffix; used both for 'all together, lock, stock, and barrel' and 'strikingly alike, the spitting image'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — そっくり

そっと.etymology: Mimetic adverb attested since Early Middle Japanese as そと / そっと, describing a quiet, gentle, unobtrusive motion or leaving something undisturbed ('softly, quietly, gently').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — そっと

その.etymology: Mesial adnominal demonstrative ('that, its, the'), inherited from Old Japanese *sono* (其の), composed of the mesial/anaphoric deictic root そ ('that') + attributive/genitive particle の.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其の

そのまま.etymology: Compound adverb and noun phrase ('just as it is, without change, immediately afterward'), combining the adnominal demonstrative その ('that') + まま (儘 'unchanged state, condition as is').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其の儘

そのもの.etymology: Compound noun phrase ('the thing itself, the very embodiment of'), combining the adnominal demonstrative その ('that, its') + もの (物 'thing, entity').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — そのもの

その一.etymology: Numbered item heading ('Part One, Number One'), combining the adnominal demonstrative その ('its, of the series') + Sino-Japanese numeral 一 (いち 'one').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — その

そば.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *soba* (側・傍 'ridge, sharp edge, side, vicinity'). From the 'edge or side of an object', it became the everyday spatial noun for 'beside, near, by someone's side' (and also named buckwheat 蕎麦 *soba* for its three-angled grain).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 側

それ.etymology: Mesial and anaphoric demonstrative pronoun ('that, that one near you, it'), inherited from Old Japanese *sore* (其れ), formed from the mesial deictic root そ ('that') + pronominal suffix -れ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其れ

それから.etymology: Conjunctive phrase ('after that, and then, since then'), composed of the demonstrative pronoun それ ('that') + ablative particle から ('from, after').

history.meaning: after that; and then; besides that

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其れから

それぞれ.etymology: Reduplicated pronoun and adverb 夫々 ('each, respectively, severally'), formed in Middle Japanese by reduplicating the demonstrative pronoun それ ('that one and that one') with rendaku voicing.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其れ其れ

それで.etymology: Conjunctive phrase ('because of that, therefore, and so'), composed of the demonstrative pronoun それ ('that') + instrumental/causal particle で ('by means of, because of').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其れで

それでも.etymology: Concessive conjunction ('even so, nevertheless, still'), composed of それで ('with that, by that') + inclusive/concessive particle も ('even').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其れでも

それと.etymology: Additive conjunction ('and also, along with that'), composed of the demonstrative pronoun それ ('that') + comitative/coordinating particle と ('and, with').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其れと

それとも.etymology: Alternative conjunction ('or, or else'), composed of それと ('with that') + inclusive particle も ('even/also'), originally elliptical for それともかくや ('or even with that, is it...').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其れとも

それなのに.etymology: Concessive conjunction ('and yet, despite that, even though that is so'), composed of それ ('that') + adnominal copula な + nominalizer の + concessive particle に ('despite').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — それなのに

それに.etymology: Additive conjunction ('moreover, besides, in addition to that'), composed of the demonstrative pronoun それ ('that') + dative/additive particle に ('to, onto').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 其れに

そんな.etymology: Mesial adnominal demonstrative ('that kind of, such a'), formed in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese by phonetic contraction of そのような (*sono yō na* 'of that manner') > そやうな > そんな.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — そんな

そんなに.etymology: Adverbial form of そんな ('so much, like that, to that extent'), formed by attaching the adverbial particle に to そんな (contracted from そのように).

history.meaning: so much; to that extent; like that

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — そんなに

ぞ.etymology: Emphatic particle inherited from Old Japanese *zo* (originally voiceless *so* in eighth-century texts, voiced to *zo* in Early Middle Japanese). Formerly a *kakari-joshi* triggering attributive verb endings, it survives as a strong sentence-final assertive particle.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ぞ

た.etymology: Past tense and perfective auxiliary suffix (-た), which evolved in Late Middle Japanese via phonetic truncation of たり (*-tari*, attributive *-taru* > *-ta*), itself a Classical Japanese fusion of the conjunctive particle て (*-te*) + existential verb あり (*ari*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — た

たい.etymology: Desiderative auxiliary adjective (-たい 'want to do'), continuing classical -たし (*-tasi*). Attested cautiously in Heian vernacular and widely from the Kamakura period onward; cognate with the standalone adjective いたし / たい ('eager, intense, painful').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — たい

たくさん.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and adverb 沢山 (たくさん 'many, a lot, plenty; enough'), originally a Middle Chinese compound meaning 'marshes and mountains' (as an image of abundance), popularized in Edo-period Japanese for 'plenty, many'.

history.form: 沢山 (たくせん / たくさん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 沢山

たたく.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tataku* (叩く・敲く 'to strike repeatedly, beat, tap, knock, clap'), attested in eighth-century texts.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 叩く

たたむ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tatamu* (畳む 'to fold up fabric or paper, pile up in layers'), the verbal source of the noun 畳 (たたみ *tatami*, originally folded rush mats).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 畳む

ただ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tada* (直・唯・只 'direct, straight, ordinary, only, merely'). In Early Modern Japanese, from 'merely as is, without extra conditions', it also developed the colloquial noun sense 'free of charge'.

history.meaning: only; simply; ordinary; free of charge

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 唯

たち.etymology: Pluralizing suffix for animate/human nouns (-たち 'and others, plural'), inherited from Old Japanese *-tati* (達), where it was a high-respect plural suffix applied to deities and royalty before broadening across pronouns and people.

history.meaning: honorific plural suffix for deities and nobles
plural suffix for people and pronouns

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 達

たった.etymology: Emphatic restrictive adverb ('only, merely, just'), evolved in Early Modern Japanese by expressive consonant gemination from ただ (唯・只 'only, just').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — たった

たった今.etymology: Emphatic temporal adverbial phrase ('just now, this very moment'), combining the restrictive intensifier たった ('just, only') + 今 (いま 'now', from Old Japanese *ima*).

history.meaning: just now; only a moment ago

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — たった今
Wiktionary — たった今 (たったいま) (Japanese)

たとえ.etymology: Concessive adverb ('even if, supposing that') and noun ('simile, comparison'), derived from the continuative stem (*tatoe*) of the Old/Middle Japanese verb たとふ (例ふ・譬ふ 'to compare, liken, suppose by analogy').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 仮令

たび.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tabi* (度 'time, occasion, occurrence'), attested in the Man'yōshū; distinct from its homophone 旅 (*tabi* 'journey'), and frequently used in 〜たびに ('every time that...').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 度

たぶん.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and modal adverb 多分 (たぶん), from 多 ('many, much') + 分 ('part, share, portion'). Originally meaning 'the greater part, majority', in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese it shifted to an epistemic adverb meaning 'in all likelihood, probably'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 多分
