たま.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tama* (偶 'rare interval, occasional chance', as in たまたま 'by chance' and たまに 'occasionally'), or its homophone 玉・球 (*tama* 'round jewel, bead, ball, sphere').

history.meaning: rare occasion (たまに); round gem or sphere
occasionally (たまの/たまに); ball, sphere, bead

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 偶

ため.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tame* (為 'benefit, sake, purpose, reason'). Originally a relational noun denoting the person or end toward which an action is directed ('sake, advantage'), it broadened to mark both purpose ('in order to') and cause ('because of').

history.meaning: for the sake of; in order to; because of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 為

だ.etymology: Plain copula formed by phonological contraction of である to であ and then だ during the Muromachi period, especially in eastern Japanese speech (with cited examples from 1473 onward).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — だ

だい.etymology: Colloquial interrogative sentence-final particle ('what is it?, who is it?'), contracted in Early Modern eastern Japanese from だ ('copula') + い (emphatic sentence-final particle); or the Sino-Japanese noun 台 (だい 'stand, platform, counter for machines').

history.form: だい (だ + い) / 台 (だい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — だい

だから.etymology: Causal conjunction ('therefore, so, that's why'), formed in Early Modern Japanese by combining the plain copula だ ('it is') + causal conjunctive particle から ('because, since').

history.meaning: because it is so; therefore; so

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — だから

だけ.etymology: Restrictive and degree particle ('only, just, as much as'), grammaticalized in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese from the native noun 丈 (たけ 'stature, height, full measure, length'). From 'to the full height/extent of', it came to mark a bounded limit ('only').

history.meaning: to the extent of; only; just

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 丈

だって.etymology: Colloquial conjunction ('but, because, after all') and concessive focus particle ('even, too'), contracted in Edo-period Japanese from だとて (*da tote* 'even if you say it is so'), combining copula だ + quotative-concessive とて.

history.meaning: even if one says it is

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — だって

だめ.etymology: Originated as the Go board-game term 駄目 (だめ 'neutral intersections between territories that yield no points for either player', combining 駄 'worthless, mere' + 目 'board intersection/point'). In Edo-period colloquial speech it generalized to 'useless, no good, forbidden'.

history.meaning: neutral/pointless intersection on a Go board

morphemes.meaning: grid point on a Go board

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 駄目

だらけ.etymology: Suffix (-だらけ 'covered in, full of, riddled with [something unwanted]'), attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese (e.g. 血だらけ 'covered in blood'); often linked to a nominalization of *daraku / darakeru* ('to drip, sprawl messily') or classical *tare-* ('dripping').

history.meaning: smeared or covered all over with
full of; covered with (dust, mistakes, etc.)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — だらけ

ちゃん.etymology: Affectionate diminutive title suffix (-ちゃん), which arose in Edo-period children's and familial speech by palatalization of the polite suffix -さん (*-san* > *-chan*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ちゃん

ちゃんと.etymology: Mimetic and manner adverb attested from the Edo period, originally imitating the crisp metallic chime or click of objects fitting into place, and hence meaning 'properly, neatly, punctual and in good order'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ちゃんと

ちょうだい.etymology: Colloquial request word ('please give me; please do') and humble verbal noun 頂戴 (ちょうだい), a Sino-Japanese compound of 頂 ('crown of the head') + 戴 ('carry on the head'), calquing the native gesture いただく ('raise a gift to the forehead when receiving').

history.meaning: humbly receiving on the crown of the head
humbly receive; 'please give me / please do'

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頂戴

ちょうちん.etymology: Borrowed in the Muromachi period from late Middle / early Mandarin Chinese *tiāodēng* (提灯 'portable hanging paper lantern', combining 提 'carry in the hand' + 灯 'lamp, lantern'), using the *tō-on* (Tang/Song–Ming) pronunciation.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 提灯

ちょうど.etymology: Originally a Late Heian / Kamakura mimetic adverb ちやうど / ちやうと imitating the solid impact of a blow or two objects meeting squarely ('squarely, right on target'). By Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese it shifted to 'precisely, exactly, just'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 丁度

ちょっと.etymology: Evolved in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese by palatalization and consonant gemination from ちと ('a little bit, briefly', cf. ちっと), describing a small amount, a brief moment, or a polite attention-getter ('just a moment, a little').

history.meaning: a little; for a moment; excuse me

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一寸

っけ.etymology: Colloquial retrospective and recall sentence-final particle (-っけ 'wasn't it?, what was it again?'), descended from the classical past/retrospective auxiliary けり (*-keri*, via eastern/colloquial *-kke*).

history.meaning: particle of trying to recall ('what was it again?')

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — っけ

って.etymology: Colloquial quotative and topic-introducing particle ('that, called, speaking of'), contracted in Early Modern Japanese from とて (*tote* 'saying that') and といって (*to itte* 'saying that').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — って

つ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *-tu*, the native Japanese numeral classifier suffix attached to the native numbers 1 through 9 (ひとつ, ふたつ ... ここのつ) and いくつ; also an archaic genitive particle ('of', preserved in まつげ 'eyelash', みなと 'harbor').

history.meaning: native general counter suffix; archaic genitive particle
counter suffix in ひとつ–ここのつ

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — つ

ついに.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *tupini* (遂に・終に 'in the end, at last; (with negative) never'), formed from the noun つひ (*tupi* 'end, final limit, completion', related to 潰ゆ / 尽く) + adverbial particle に.

history.meaning: until the end; finally; (with negative) never
finally; at last; in the end

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 遂に

つかまる.etymology: Intransitive verb 捕まる・掴まる ('to be caught; to hold on tightly to'), paired with 掴む (*tukamu* 'to grasp, seize') and 捕まえる (*tukamaeru* 'to catch, arrest'), attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese.

history.form: つかまる (捕まる・掴まる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 捕まる

つく.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tuku*, representing several core verbs including 付く・着く ('to attach, stick to, arrive at, turn on [of lights]') and 突く ('to thrust, poke, strike a bell').

history.form: つく (付く・着く / 突く)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 付く

つける.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) transitive verb 付ける・着ける ('to attach, apply, put on, turn on a light, season/soak 漬ける'), continuing Old Japanese *tuku* (transitive counterpart of four-grade *tuku* 'to stick, arrive').

history.form: つく (付く・着く, lower bigrade)

history.meaning: attach; put on; turn on; keep (a record)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 付ける

つながる.etymology: Intransitive verb 繋がる ('to be connected, linked, tied together, get through by phone'), derived in Middle Japanese from つなぐ (繋ぐ 'to tie, tether') + intransitive suffix -ある (*-aru*).

history.meaning: be tied together; form a continuous link
be connected; be linked; lead to

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 繋がる

つなぐ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tunagu* (繋ぐ 'to tie with a rope, tether, connect, join'), verbalized from the noun 綱 (つな *tuna* 'rope, cord, tether').

history.meaning: fasten with a tether; tie; link

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 繋ぐ

つもり.etymology: Verbal noun 積もり ('intention, plan, expectation'), nominalized from the continuative stem of 積もる (*tumoru* 'to pile up, accumulate; estimate/calculate by piling up'). From 'mental estimate or calculation', it shifted in Early Modern Japanese to 'one's intention or plan'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 積もり

つる草.etymology: Native Japanese botanical compound 蔓草 (つるくさ 'climbing vine, creeper'), combining つる (蔓 'vine, tendril, runner', from Old Japanese *turu*, cognate with 弦 'bowstring') + 草 (くさ 'grass, herbaceous plant').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 蔓草

て.etymology: Conjunctive particle (-て) linking sequential actions, means, or states, inherited from Old Japanese *-te*, which grammaticalized from the continuative stem (*-te*) of the perfective auxiliary つ (*-tu* 'to finish doing').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — て

ても.etymology: Concessive conjunctive particle ('even if, although'), formed by combining the conjunctive particle て (-て) + the inclusive/concessive focus particle も ('even').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ても

で.etymology: Case particle marking location of action, instrument/means, cause, or material ('at, in, by, with'), which arose in Late Heian and Kamakura Japanese via phonetic fusion of にて (*ni te*, locative particle に + conjunctive て). Also serves as the continuative (*-te*) form of the copula だ.

history.meaning: at; in; by means of (being at)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — で

できる.etymology: Upper bigrade/ichidan verb 出来る ('to come into existence, be completed, be able to do'), contracted in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese from 出で来る (*idekuru* 'to come forth, appear, emerge', combining 出づ 'come out' + 来る 'come').

history.form: いでく / いでくる (出で来)

history.meaning: be made/ready; be able to do

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 出来る

です.etymology: Polite copula documented from the Muromachi period onward that spread across general polite speech in the late Edo and Meiji periods. Reference dictionaries list several proposed contractions—including で候 (de sōrō), でおはす, でございます, and であります—without consensus on a single source.

history.meaning: stylized copular ending in dramatic and social registers

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — です

でないと.etymology: Conditional connective ('otherwise, if not, unless'), formed from でない ('is not', composed of copular で + negative ない) + conditional particle と ('when, if').

history.meaning: if it is not so; otherwise

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — でないと

では.etymology: Conjunction ('well then, in that case') and compound particle, formed from the locative/copular particle で + topic/contrastive particle は. Source of colloquial じゃあ.

history.meaning: in/at (with contrast); well then; if so

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — では

でも.etymology: Concessive conjunction ('but, however, even so') and focus particle ('even, or something like'), formed from the copular/case particle で + inclusive particle も ('even').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — でも

と.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *to*, serving since eighth-century texts as the comitative and coordinating particle ('with, and'), the quotative particle ('that, thus'), and the natural-consequence conditional particle ('when, whenever').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — と

という.etymology: Appositive and clause-linking expression ('called, that, namely'), composed of the quotative particle と + the verb いう (言う 'to say, call').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — と言う

とおり.etymology: Verbal noun 通り ('street, passage; manner, just as'), nominalized from the continuative stem of 通る (*tooru* 'to pass through, go along', from Old Japanese *toporu*).

history.meaning: street; avenue; in accordance with; just as

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 通り

とか.etymology: Non-exhaustive listing and quotative uncertainty particle ('things like ... and ...; I hear that'), formed from the quotative/coordinating particle と + question/indefinite particle か.

history.meaning: something to the effect of; things like ... and ...

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — とか

とかいう.etymology: Compound adnominal phrase ('called something like..., someone by the name of...'), combining the indefinite quotative particle とか ('something like') + いう (言う 'to say, call').

history.meaning: called something like; or whatever it is called

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — とか言う
Wiktionary — とかいう (とか言う) (Japanese)

とき.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *toki* (時 'time, hour, season, occasion, when'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; used both as a standalone noun and as a temporal clause head ('when...').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 時

ところ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tokoro* (所・処 'place, spot, locality'), likely built on the spatial root *to* ('place', as in あと, そと) + extended suffix *-koro*. Grammaticalized also to mark temporal aspect ('just about to, in the midst of, just finished').

history.meaning: place; point; aspectual 'just now / about to'

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 所

として.etymology: Compound particle ('as, in the capacity of, taking as'), formed from the quotative/essives particle と + して (the *-te* form of する 'to treat as, make').

history.meaning: treating as; in the role/capacity of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — として

とても.etymology: Originally an Early and Late Middle Japanese adverb とて (with inclusive も) shortened from とてもかくても ('whether this way or that way, no matter how'), used with negative predicates to mean 'by no means, cannot possibly'. In the Meiji–Taishō era it generalized to affirmative sentences as 'very, awfully, extremely'.

history.meaning: either way; (with negative) by no means

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 迚も

とにかく.etymology: Idiomatic adverb 兎に角 ('anyway, at any rate, first of all'), shortened from the classical phrase とにもかくにも ('whether this way [と] or that way [かく]'). The kanji 兎に角 are Edo/Meiji playful phonetic ateji.

history.meaning: whether that way or this way
anyway; in any case; at any rate

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 兎に角

とも.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tomo*, functioning both as a concessive conjunctive particle ('even if, no matter') and as a noun/suffix 共 ('both, together, including; humble plural'). Also combines quotative と + も ('certainly, of course').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 共

とんでもない.etymology: Emphatic adjective ('unthinkable, outrageous, by no means, don't mention it!'), formed in Early Modern Japanese from 途方もない (*tohō mo nai* 'without rhyme, reason, or direction') or 飛んでもない ('not even by a wild leap'), expressing strong denial or astonishment.

history.meaning: extraordinary; unthinkable; out of the question
unthinkable; outrageous; 'not at all / don't mention it'

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — とんでもない

どう.etymology: Interrogative manner adverb ('how, in what way'), which evolved in Late Middle Japanese via *u*-onbin (*dau* > *dō*) from ど- (the interrogative root seen in どこ, どれ, どの, which replaced older いづ-) + adverbial ending -う (patterned after こう, そう, ああ).

history.meaning: how; in what way; how about

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 如何

どうして.etymology: Interrogative adverb ('why, how, by what means'), formed from the manner interrogative どう ('how') + して (the *-te* form of する 'to do'), literally 'doing how?'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 如何して

どうせ.etymology: Modal adverb ('anyway, in any case, after all'), shortened in Edo-period Japanese from どうせうとも ('no matter how one may do it') or どうせう ('how shall we do -> either way').

history.meaning: no matter what; in any event; after all
anyway; after all; at any rate

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — どうせ

どうぞ.etymology: Polite adverb of request or invitation ('please, go ahead, by all means'), formed in Late Middle / Early Modern Japanese from どう ('how, in some way') + emphatic particle ぞ. Originally meaning 'somehow or other, by all means', it specialized into a polite invitation ('please').

history.meaning: please; go right ahead; here you are

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 何卒

どうも.etymology: Adverb and versatile conversational greeting ('somehow, very much, thanks, hello'), formed in Early Modern Japanese from どう ('how') + inclusive particle も ('even/in every way'). From 'no matter how one tries [to express thanks/apology]', it became a polite all-purpose acknowledgement.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — どうも

どうやって.etymology: Interrogative manner phrase ('how, by doing what'), composed of どう ('how') + やって (the *-te* form of やる 'to do, perform').

history.meaning: by doing how; in what way

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — どう

どきどき.etymology: Reduplicated mimetic adverb attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese (related to どきりと), imitating the heavy thumping or pounding of the heart from excitement, anticipation, fear, or exertion.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — どきどき

どこ.etymology: Interrogative spatial pronoun ('where, what place'), which evolved in Late Heian and Kamakura Japanese by phonetic reduction from Old Japanese いづこ (*iduko* > *duko* > *doko*), composed of interrogative root いづ- + locative *-ko*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 何処

どころか.etymology: Compound particle ('far from, let alone, on the contrary'), grammaticalized in Early Modern Japanese from the noun どころ (voiced from ところ 所 'place, point, situation') + question/rhetorical particle か: 'is it a matter of X? [No, far beyond that!]'.

history.meaning: far from being the case of; let alone
far from; not to mention; on the contrary

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 所か

どちら.etymology: Polite interrogative directional and selective pronoun ('which way, where, which of the two, who'), formed in Middle Japanese from the interrogative root ど- (from older いづ-) + directional suffix -ちら (parallel to こちら, そちら, あちら).

history.meaning: which way; where; which one; who (polite)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 何方

どなた.etymology: Polite interrogative personal pronoun ('who, which person'), evolved in Middle Japanese from older いづかた / どかた (何方 'which direction, which personage') via nasal assimilation (*donata*), parallel to あなた ('you') and こなた.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 何方

どの.etymology: Interrogative adnominal determiner ('which, what'), evolved in Late Heian and Kamakura Japanese from Old Japanese いづれの (*idure no*) / いづの (*idu no*) via phonetic reduction to どの (parallel to この, その, あの).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — どの

どんどん.etymology: Reduplicated onomatopoeic and mimetic adverb originally imitating the booming beat of drums (どんと) or rushing water, and by extension describing actions or changes proceeding rapidly and steadily ('steadily, rapidly, one after another').

history.meaning: booming of drums; rapidly and continuously

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — どんどん

どんな.etymology: Interrogative adnominal determiner ('what kind of, what sort of'), contracted in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese from どのような (*dono yō na* 'of what manner') > どやうな > どんな (parallel to こんな, そんな, あんな).

history.meaning: what kind of; what sort of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — どんな

な.etymology: Multifunctional particle and copular inflection: (1) sentence-final emotive/exclamatory particle inherited from Old Japanese *na* (なあ); (2) prohibitive sentence-final particle ('do not!') from Old Japanese *na*; and (3) the adnominal form of the copula だ (reduced in Late Middle Japanese from なる *naru*).

history.form: な (emotive / prohibitive) and なる (adnominal copula)

history.meaning: sentence-final particle; prohibitive particle; na-adjective linker

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — な

ない.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *nasi* (無し, attributive *naki* > *nai* 'non-existent, not having, not'). Also functions as the standard negative auxiliary adjective attached to the irrealis (*mizenkei*) stem of verbs and adjectives.

history.form: なし (無し, attributive なき)

history.meaning: there is no; not have; negative auxiliary

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無い

ながら.etymology: Conjunctive particle ('while doing, although, as it is'), inherited from Old Japanese *nagara* (originally attached to nouns, e.g. 神ながら 'as a deity is', likely related to 流る / なか 'flow, nature, course'). Later extended to verb continuative stems to express simultaneous action ('while').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 乍ら

なくす.etymology: Compound transitive verb 無くす ('to lose, get rid of, do away with'), formed from 無く (adverbial form of ない 'non-existent') + classical する / す ('to make, cause to be').

history.meaning: cause to be gone; lose; eliminate

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無くす

なくなる.etymology: Compound intransitive verb 無くなる・亡くなる ('to disappear, run out, be lost; to pass away'), formed from 無く (adverbial form of ない 'non-existent') + なる (成る 'to become').

history.meaning: run out; go missing; pass away

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無くなる

なさる.etymology: Honorific verb 為さる ('to deign to do'), evolved in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese from 為さる (*nasaru*, passive/honorific derivation of なす 為す 'to do, make, accomplish'). Source of the polite imperative なさい.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 為さる

なし.etymology: Noun and suffix 無し ('without, none, free of'), preserving the classical conclusive (*shūshikei*) form なし of the adjective ない (無し 'non-existent'). Also homophonous with 梨 (なし 'Japanese pear', from Old Japanese *nasi*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無し

なじむ.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *nadimu* (馴染む 'to become familiar with, grow accustomed to, blend in harmonically'), related to なづむ / なつく ('to become attached or tame').

history.meaning: blend in well (flavors, materials); become familiar with

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 馴染む

なめらか.etymology: Adjectival noun 滑らか ('smooth, sleek, fluent'), formed in Old and Early Middle Japanese from the root *name-* (seen in 滑る *nameru* 'to slip, glide smoothly') + adjectival suffix -らか ('having the state/appearance of').

history.meaning: smooth to the touch; sleek; fluent

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 滑らか

なら.etymology: Conditional particle and copular form ('if it is, as for, if'), shortened in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese from ならば (*naraba*), the irrealis conditional form of the classical copula なり (*nari* 'to be').

history.meaning: if it be the case that
if; in the case of; as for

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — なら

なる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *naru*, attested in eighth-century texts for coming into being, bearing fruit, and changing into another state. Its modern everyday sense 'become' continues that core change-of-state meaning.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 成る

なるほど.etymology: Adverb and interjection of agreement ('I see, indeed, that makes sense'), grammaticalized from the phrase 成る程 (*naru hodo* 'to the extent that is possible / as much as it becomes'). From 'to the fullest possible degree', it shifted in the Edo period to 'just as you say, indeed, I see'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 成る程

なれる.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) verb 慣れる・馴れる, continuing Old Japanese *naru* ('to grow accustomed to, become tame, become practiced or worn in with use').

history.meaning: grow familiar; become accustomed or tame
get used to; become experienced in

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 慣れる

なんか.etymology: Colloquialexemplifying and softening particle ('things like, someone like, or something'), contracted in Early Modern and Modern Japanese from なんか < なにか (何か 'something') and などか ('things like').

history.form: なにか / などか → なんか

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — なんか
Wiktionary — なにか / などか → なんか (Japanese)

なんだか.etymology: Adverb ('somehow, for some reason, kind of'), formed from なんだ (contracted from なにだ 'what it is') + indefinite question particle か ('somehow, without knowing quite what').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 何だか

なんて.etymology: Colloquial quotative, exclamatory, and belittling/exemplifying particle ('such a thing as, that..., what a...!'), contracted in Early Modern Japanese from なんといって (*nan to itte* 'saying what') or などとて (*nado tote*).

history.form: なんといふ / などとて → なんて
history.meaning: things called; such a thing as

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — なんて

なんと.etymology: Exclamatory and interrogative adverb ('what a...!, how...!, surprisingly'), formed from the interrogative pronoun なに > なん (何 'what') + particle と.

history.meaning: how; what a...!; to one's surprise

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 何と

に.etymology: Core Japanese case particle attested throughout eighth-century Man'yōshū poetry, marking points in time, static locations of existence, destinations, and indirect recipients.

history.meaning: marks location, time, goal, and recipient

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — に

におい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *nipopi* (匂い・臭い), nominalized from the verb *nipopu* (匂ふ). In Old Japanese (Man'yōshū), *nipopu* meant 'to shine with warm, vivid color (especially red)'; in Heian court culture (famous for incense blending) it shifted to 'fragrance, aroma', and later to any 'smell, scent, odor'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 匂い
Wiktionary — におい (匂い・臭い) (Japanese)

にぎやか.etymology: Adjectival noun 賑やか ('lively, bustling, cheerful'), formed from the root *nigi-* (seen in Old Japanese *nigipapu* / 賑わう 'to flourish, be abundant and prosperous', related to 和 *nigi* 'gentle, harmonious, plentiful') + adjectival suffix -やか.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 賑やか

にこにこ.etymology: Reduplicated mimetic adverb attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese (built on the ancient root *niko-* 'soft, gentle, smiling', seen in Old Japanese *nikoyaka* and *nikoniko*), describing a warm, cheerful smile.

history.form: にこやか / にこにこ

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — にこにこ

にとって.etymology: Compound postpositional particle ('for, from the standpoint of, to'), grammaticalized from dative particle に + とって (the *-te* form of 取る *toru* 'to take, adopt as a viewpoint').

history.form: にとりて → にとって

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — に取って
Wiktionary — にとりて → にとって (Japanese)

によって.etymology: Compound postpositional particle ('by means of, due to, depending on, according to'), grammaticalized from dative particle に + よって (the *-te* form of 依る・因る・拠る *yoru* 'to depend on, be based on, be caused by').

history.form: によりて → によって (に因って・に依って)
history.meaning: owing to; by means of; depending on

morphemes.part: よって (因って・依って)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — に因って
Wiktionary — によりて → によって (に因って・に依って) (Japanese)

にんじん.etymology: Originally the Sino-Japanese name 人参 (にんじん 'ginseng', literally 'human-shaped root', fromの人 'person' + 参 'ginseng'). When the culinary carrot (*Daucus carota*) entered Japan in the 16th–17th centuries, it was called せりにんじん ('parsley-ginseng') for its similar root and foliage, soon shortening to にんじん.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 人参

ぬる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *nuru* (塗る 'to spread, apply paint/plaster/jam, coat, smear'), attested in eighth-century texts; cognate with 濡る ('to get wet') from the shared sense of liquid adhering to a surface.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塗る

ぬるい.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *nurusi* (温し・微温し 'lukewarm, tepid; lax, slow'), describing water or liquid that is neither hot nor cold.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 温い

ぬるま湯.etymology: Native Japanese compound ぬるま湯 ('lukewarm water, tepid bath'), combining the adjective stem ぬる- (from ぬるい 'lukewarm') + element -ま- (interval/state, as in ぬるま) + 湯 (ゆ 'hot/warm water').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 微温湯
Wiktionary — ぬるまゆ (ぬるま湯) (Japanese)

ね.etymology: Sentence-final conversational particle documented from late Edo speech (with dictionary citations from 1788), used to invite agreement, confirm shared information, or soften a statement.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ね

ねえ.etymology: Lengthened form of the sentence-final and interjectional particle ね (derived from earlier な / なあ), used either to call someone's attention ('hey, say, listen') or to seek warm agreement ('isn't it?, right?').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ねえ

ねじ.etymology: Noun 螺子・捻じ ('screw, spiral thread, clockwork spring'), nominalized from the continuative stem (*nedi* > *neji*) of the Old/Middle Japanese verb ねづ / ねじる (捻じる 'to twist, wrench, turn spirally').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 螺子

の.etymology: Native Japanese genitive and noun-linking particle already attested in the Kojiki (712). Over time it also developed a nominalizing function turning clauses into noun-like statements; in modern spoken Japanese, explanatory の before です or だ frequently contracts to ん.

history.meaning: links a modifying noun to a following noun

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — の

のか.etymology: Compound sentence-final particle expressing an explanatory question or realization ('is it that...?, oh, so...!'), formed from the explanatory nominalizer の + question particle か.

history.meaning: is it the case that...?; oh, so that's why

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — のか

のぞく.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *nozoku* (覗く・臨く 'to peer into, peek through a gap, look down from an edge'), alongside homophonous 除く (*nozoku* 'to remove, exclude, omit').

history.meaning: lean over to look in; peek / remove

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 覗く

ので.etymology: Causal conjunctive particle ('because, since'), formed in Early Modern Japanese by combining the clause-nominalizing particle の + the instrumental/causal copular particle で ('it being the fact that...').

history.meaning: because of the fact that; since

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ので

のに.etymology: Concessive conjunctive particle ('although, even though, despite') and purpose/context marker ('for doing'), formed in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese from the nominalizing particle の + dative/locative particle に ('in the situation where...').

history.meaning: in the circumstance that -> even though; in order to
although; despite; for the purpose of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — のに

は.etymology: Topic and contrastive particle (pronounced *wa*, spelled は), inherited from Old Japanese *pa*. By the Heian–Kamakura periods, intervocalic *-p-* lenited to *-w-* (*pa* > *wa*), while classical orthography retained the kana は for the particle.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — は

はあ.etymology: Lengthened native Japanese interjection representing either a polite/tentative acknowledgment ('yes, I see'), puzzled wonder ('huh?'), or an audible sigh/exhalation ('ah, phew').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — はあ

はい.etymology: Standard polite affirmative response ('yes, here, present'), which arose in Edo-period Japanese from earlier はい / はあ (possibly linked to 拝 *hai* 'bowing in respect' or a vocalic shift from medieval affirmative へい / おう).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — はい

はがき.etymology: Native Japanese compound 葉書 (はがき), from 葉 (は, 'leaf, small slip') and 書き (かき -> -がき by rendaku, 'writing').
はがき.notes: Originally referred to brief notes jotted on single slips of paper (端書き / 葉書き), standardized for postal cards in modern Japan.

はじめまして.etymology: Standard greeting on meeting someone for the first time ('nice to meet you, how do you do'), literally the polite *-masu* + *-te* form of 始める (*hajimeru* 'to begin'): 'beginning [our acquaintance] for the first time, [I greet you]'.

history.form: はじめまして (始めまして)

history.meaning: how do you do; nice to meet you

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 始めまして

はず.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *padu* (筈 'the nock at the end of an arrow that fits onto the bowstring, or the tip of a bow where the string notches'). Because the arrow nock and bowstring must fit together precisely, in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese はず came to mean 'natural fit, logical expectation, supposed to be'.

history.meaning: notch of an arrow or bow tip
fitting expectation; supposed to be; bound to

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 筈

はっきり.etymology: Mimetic adverb attested from the Edo period, formed on a root *haki-* (related to はきはき 'briskly, clearly' and 明く *aku* 'to open, grow bright/clear') with gemination and *-ri* suffix, meaning 'clearly, distinctly, definitely'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — はっきり

はは.etymology: Onomatopoeic interjection representing light, open-mouthed laughter ('haha'), alongside the homophonous kinship noun 母 (はは 'mother', inherited from Old Japanese *papa*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — はは

はまる.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *pamaru* (嵌まる・填まる 'to plunge into, fit snugly into a groove or socket, fall into a trap'), intransitive counterpart of はめる (*hameru*). In modern colloquial Japanese it also means 'to get hooked on, be absorbed in'.

history.meaning: plunge into; fall in; fit inside
fit snugly into; get stuck in; be hooked on

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 嵌まる

ばかり.etymology: Restrictive and approximative particle ('only, just, about, just finished doing'), grammaticalized in Old and Early Middle Japanese from ばかり (計り・量り, nominalized stem of はかる *pakaru* 'to measure, weigh, estimate').

history.form: はかり → ばかり (計り)

history.meaning: only; just; about; having just done (~たばかり)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 許り

ばっちり.etymology: Mimetic adverb with voiced initial *ba-* (related to ぱっちり 'wide-open eyes; clicking shut'), popularized in modern colloquial Japanese for something hitting the mark or working out impeccably ('perfectly, spot-on, right on target').

history.form: ぱっちり / ばっちり

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ばっちり

ひそめる.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) transitive verb 潜める ('to hide, conceal, lower one's voice') and 顰める ('to knit or furrow one's brows'), continuing Old/Early Middle Japanese *pisomu*.

history.meaning: conceal; quiet down; knit the brows

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 潜める

ひだまり旅館.etymology: Compound proper name ('Hidamari Ryokan / Sunny Spot Inn'), combining native 日だまり (ひだまり 'sunny sheltered spot where warmth gathers', from 日 *hi* 'sun' + 溜まり *damari* 'gathering place') + Sino-Japanese 旅館 (りょかん 'traditional Japanese inn', from 旅 'travel' + 館 'lodging hall').

history.form: ひだまり (日溜まり) + 旅館 (りょかん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 日溜まり

ひとさじ.etymology: Hybrid numeral-classifier compound 一匙 (ひとさじ 'one spoonful'), combining native numeral prefix ひと- (一 'one') + 匙 (さじ 'spoon, scoop', an old borrowing from Middle Chinese *dzyeX* 匙 'spoon').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一匙

ひとつまみ.etymology: Native Japanese culinary measurement compound 一摘まみ (ひとつまみ 'a pinch [of salt, spice]'), combining ひと- (一 'one') + つまみ (摘まみ, nominalized stem of つまむ 'to pinch between the fingertips').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一摘まみ
Wiktionary — ひとつまみ (一摘まみ) (Japanese)

ひどい.etymology: Adjective 非道い・酷い ('harsh, severe, awful, excessive, cruel'), which arose in Early Modern Japanese by reanalyzing the Sino-Japanese noun 非道 (*hidō* 'unjust, outrageous, contrary to the way') as a native *-i* adjective (*hido-i*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 酷い

ひねる.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *pineru* (捻る・拈る 'to twist with the fingers, turn a knob/faucet, wrack one's brains'), attested in Heian literature.

history.meaning: twist; turn (a tap/switch); devise a clever twist

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 捻る

ひび.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pibi* (皹・罅 'fine crack, fissure in pottery, wood, or chapped skin'), cognate with the verb ひびく (響く 'to reverberate, jar, crack from vibration'). Also homophonous with 日々 (ひび 'day by day, daily').

history.meaning: chapped skin; hairline crack in a vessel
crack; fissure (in glass, ceramic, or wall)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 罅

びしょ濡れ.etymology: Compound noun びしょ濡れ ('soaking wet, drenched'), combining the mimetic root びしょ (from びしょびしょ 'dripping wet, sodden') + 濡れ (ぬれ, nominalized stem of 濡れる 'to get wet').

history.form: びしょぬれ (びしょ濡れ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — びしょ濡れ
Wiktionary — びしょぬれ (びしょ濡れ) (Japanese)

びっくり.etymology: Mimetic adverb attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese (related to びくっと / びくびく 'startling, twitching'), formed with gemination and *-ri* suffix to express sudden startle or astonishment ('surprised, startled').

history.meaning: with a sudden startle or jolt

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 吃驚

ぴかぴか.etymology: Reduplicated mimetic adverb built on the light/flash root *pika-* (related to 光る *hikaru* 'to shine', retaining archaic/expressive initial bilabial/stop *p-*), describing a bright, polished, or freshly sparkling surface ('sparkling, shiny, brand-new').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ぴかぴか

ぴったり.etymology: Mimetic adverb and adjectival noun attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese (alongside ぴたり), built on the root *pita-* ('pressing flat against, adhering closely', cf. ひたと) + gemination and *-ri* suffix: 'snugly, closely, exactly on the mark'.

history.meaning: snugly; exactly; fitting to a T

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ぴったり

ぴんと.etymology: Mimetic adverb with expressive *p-* initial, describing either a cord, cloth, or posture stretched taut ('tautly, tensely') or an immediate flash of intuition (ぴんとくる 'to click, catch on instantly').

history.meaning: stretched taut; with a sharp click of intuition

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ぴんと

ふう.etymology: Onomatopoeic interjection representing a long, audible breath blown out in relief, fatigue, or calming down ('phew, whew'), or the Sino-Japanese noun 風 (ふう 'manner, style, way, appearance').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ふう

ふた.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *puta* (蓋 'lid, cover, cap'), attested in eighth-century texts; also the native numeral stem ふた- (二 'two').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 蓋

ふふ.etymology: Onomatopoeic interjection representing a soft, breathy chuckle or quiet laugh ('hehe, hmph').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ふふ

ぶつける.etymology: Colloquial transitive verb ぶつける ('to bump into, knock against, throw at, vent'), formed in Early Modern Japanese from emphatic prefix ぶっ- (from 打つ *utsu* 'to strike, hit') + つける (付ける・着ける 'to bring into contact, Dash against').

history.form: ぶっつける → ぶつける

history.meaning: bump (one's head/knee); hit against; throw at

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 打付ける

へ.etymology: Allative case particle (pronounced *e*, spelled へ 'toward, to'), grammaticalized in Old Japanese from the spatial noun へ (辺 *pe* 'side, vicinity, shore, direction'). Intervocalic lenition shifted *pe* > *we* > *e* in the Heian period while preserving the spelling へ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — へ

べき.etymology: Deontic modal auxiliary ('should, ought to, must'), preserving the classical attributive (*rentaikei*) form べき of the Old/Classical Japanese auxiliary べし (*besi* 'bound to, fitting to, ought to', likely related to 宜 *ube* 'fitting, natural').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — べき

べたつく.etymology: Intransitive verb べたつく ('to be sticky, feel clammy or tacky'), formed from the mimetic root べた- (from べたべた 'sticky, smeared all over') + verbalizing suffix -つく.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — べたつく

ほう.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 方 (ほう 'direction, side, way, alternative in comparison'), borrowed from Middle Chinese *pjang* (方 'square, direction, side, method'). Used in comparative constructions (〜のほうが 'the side of... -> more...').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 方

ほこり.etymology: Noun 埃 ('fine dust floating in the air or settling on surfaces'), attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese; derived from the verb ほこる (*hokoru* 'to rise up, billow, spread out'), describing dust motes billowing in the air.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 埃

ほしい.etymology: Descends from Old Japanese adjective *fosi* (classical ほし), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū in the sense of 'desirable, wanted'. Modern ほしい (欲しい) generalized the attributive *-ki > -i* ending, and the auxiliary request pattern 〜てほしい is attested by 1686.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 欲しい

ほっと.etymology: Mimetic adverb imitating a warm sigh of relief exhaled after tension or worry passes ('with a sigh of relief, relieved'), attested from Early Modern Japanese (e.g. ほっと息をつく).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ほっと

ほとんど.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *potopoto* (殆ど 'nearly, on the verge of'), which underwent nasalization and voicing in Early Middle Japanese (*potopoto* > *potondo* > *hotondo*), meaning 'almost, nearly, for the most part'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 殆ど

ほど.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *podo* (程 'interval of time or space, degree, limit, extent'). Grammaticalized as a particle indicating approximate amount ('about, around'), upper bound/comparison ('to the extent of'), and proportional correlation (〜ば〜ほど 'the more... the more').

history.meaning: span of time or space; degree; social station
extent; degree; about; as much as

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 程

ほめる.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) verb 褒める・誉める, continuing Old Japanese *pomu* ('to praise, extol, celebrate with words of blessing').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 褒める

ほら.etymology: Attention-calling interjection ('look!, see!, there you go!'), evolved in Early Modern Japanese alongside そら and あら as a deictic call directing the listener's eyes or attention to something immediate.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ほら

ほんの.etymology: Adnominal determiner ('mere, only a slight, just a token'), formed in Early Modern Japanese from Sino-Japanese 本 (ほん 'original, basic, slight starting point') + attributive particle の.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本の

まあ.etymology: Interjection and modal adverb ('well, my!, for now, more or less'), formed by lengthening the syllable ま (seen in まあまあ), expressing mild surprise ('oh my!') or moderate qualification ('well, passably, for the moment').

history.meaning: exclamation of surprise or moderate concession
well; more or less; oh my!

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — まあ

まさか.etymology: Originally the Old Japanese noun まさか (正処 / 目前 'the actual present moment, when the critical moment arrives', from まさ 'real, right now' + か 'place/time'). Used with negative predicates ('even if it came to the critical moment, surely not'), it became an adverb and interjection meaning 'surely not, by no means, no way!'.

history.meaning: surely not; no way!; in an emergency (まさかの時)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 真逆

まさに.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *masani* (正に・将に), formed from the adjectival root まさ (正 'true, exact, right') + adverbial particle に. Used both for exactness ('truly,まさに, precisely') and imminent aspect ('just about to', calquing Classical Chinese 将).

history.meaning: precisely; truly; right on the verge of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 正に

ます.etymology: Polite verbal auxiliary suffix (-ます), grammaticalized through progressive phonological reduction from the Late Heian / Kamakura humble verb まゐらす (参らす 'to offer up, perform humbly for a superior') > まるらす > まらす > まする > ます.

history.form: まゐらす (参らす) → まらす → まする
history.meaning: humbly do for a respected person

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ます

まず.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *madu* (先づ, spelled まづ in historical kana), derived from the root *ma-* (前 'front, before, ahead') + directional/adverbial suffix *-du*: 'first of all, before anything else, to begin with'.

history.meaning: first of all; to begin with; for now

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 先ず

まずは.etymology: Discourse adverbial ('first of all, for a start, at any rate'), formed from the adverb まず (先ず 'first') + topic/contrastive particle は.

history.meaning: first of all; for the time being

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 先ずは

また.etymology: Native adverb attested in the Nihon Shoki (720) meaning 'again, once more', later extending to 'also' and 'on another occasion'—the sense underlying everyday farewells like またね ('see you again') and また明日 ('see you tomorrow').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 又

またね.etymology: Casual parting greeting ('see you again, bye for now'), elliptical for また会いましょうね ('let's meet again, okay?'), combining また (又 'again, next time') + sentence-final particle ね.

history.meaning: see you later!; until next time

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 又

また明日.etymology: Parting greeting ('see you tomorrow'), elliptical for また明日会いましょう ('let's meet again tomorrow'), combining また (又 'again') + 明日 (あした 'tomorrow', originally 'morning' from 明けし朝, which shifted in Late Middle Japanese to 'tomorrow').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 明日

まだ.etymology: Temporal adverb ('still, yet; (with negative) not yet'), which evolved in Early Middle and Late Middle Japanese by apheresis (loss of initial *i-*) from Old Japanese いまだ (*imada* 未だ 'up to now, still', built on いま 'now').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 未だ

まっすぐ.etymology: Emphatic adjectival noun and adverb 真っ直ぐ ('straight ahead, direct, upright, honest'), formed from the intensive prefix まっ- (真 'true, pure, right') + すぐ (直ぐ 'straight, direct').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 真っ直ぐ

まったく.etymology: Adverb 全く ('completely, entirely; (with negative) not at all; good grief'), the adverbial (*ren'yōkei*) form of the Old/Classical Japanese adjective 全し (*matasi* / *mattasi* 'complete, intact, whole, lacking nothing').

history.form: またし / まったく (全く)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 全く

まで.etymology: Terminative particle ('until, as far as, to, even'), inherited from Old Japanese *made* (迄), attested in eighth-century texts for spatial and temporal limits ('all the way to').

history.meaning: as far as; until; to the degree of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 迄

まま.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mama* (儘・随 'as it is, following the natural state or will of'), attested in the Man'yōshū; used as a formal noun after verbs and modifiers to indicate an unchanged or ongoing state.

history.meaning: in accordance with; just as it is
as it is; remaining in that state

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 儘

みたい.etymology: Colloquial evidential and similative auxiliary ('like, similar to, seems to be'), contracted in late Edo and Meiji Tokyo Japanese from 見たよう (*mita yō* 'the appearance of having seen -> looks like').

history.meaning: like; similar to; appears to be

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — みたい

みる.etymology: Upper monograde (ichidan) verb 見る ('to see, look at, watch, check'), continuing Old Japanese *miru*. Following the *-te* form of another verb (〜てみる), it functions as an auxiliary meaning 'to try doing and see what happens'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 見る

みんな.etymology: Pronoun and adverb ('everyone, all, everything'), formed in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese by expressive nasal gemination from みな (皆 'all, everyone', inherited from Old Japanese *mina*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 皆

むずむず.etymology: Reduplicated mimetic adverb attested from Early Modern Japanese, describing a creepy-crawly tickling, itching, or restless urge ('itchy, ticklish, itching to do something').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — むずむず

むっと.etymology: Mimetic adverb attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese, describing either a sudden flash of sullen anger/offense ('huffily, sullenly') or a stifling, close wave of heat or scent ('stiflingly, overwhelmingly').

history.meaning: flaring up in silent displeasure; stiflingly

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — むっと

も.etymology: Inclusive focus particle ('also, too, even, both... and...'), inherited unchanged from Old Japanese *mo* since the earliest eighth-century inscriptions and poetry.

history.meaning: also; too; even; as many as

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — も

もう.etymology: Aspectual and degree adverb ('already, soon, now; another, more') and emotive exclamation ('gee, come on!'), which evolved in Late Middle Japanese from まう < いま (今 'now, further') or by vocalization of もはや ('already').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — もう

もし.etymology: Suppositional adverb ('if, in case, supposing'), inherited from Old Japanese *mosi* (若し・もし), used in correlation with conditional verb forms (〜ば, 〜たら, 〜なら) to introduce a hypothesis.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 若し

もしもし.etymology: Standard telephone and attention-getting greeting ('hello?, excuse me'), formed by reduplicating もし, which contracted in Edo-period speech from 申し (*mōshi*, continuative stem of the humble verb 申す *mōsu* 'to say, speak to a superior'). Popularized in 1890 when Japan's first telephone service began.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — もしもし

もちろん.etymology: Sino-Japanese adverb 勿論 (もちろん 'of course, needless to say'), borrowed from Chinese 勿論 (combining prohibitive 勿 'do not, need not' + 論 'discuss, argue, debate': 'there is no need even to debate it').

history.meaning: of course; naturally; needless to say

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 勿論

もっと.etymology: Comparative degree adverb ('more, further, even more'), which arose in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese by expressive gemination from もと (originally linked to もうと / いまひと 'one more degree' or 本 *moto*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — もっと

もの.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mono* (物 'concrete thing, object, substance' and 者 'person'). Also grammaticalized as a formal noun and sentence-final explanatory/emotive particle ('because, after all; used to').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 物

もらう.etymology: Inherited from Late Middle Japanese もらふ (貰う 'to receive, get from someone'), originally meaning 'to beg food or alms, have someone bestow upon one' (possibly related to 漏る 'trickle down' or 盛る 'serve'). After a *-te* verb (〜てもらう), it marks having someone do a favor.

history.meaning: receive; get; have someone do (~てもらう)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 貰う

もらえる.etymology: Potential form of もらう (貰う 'to receive'), meaning 'can receive, be able to get' or used in polite requests ('could I get you to...').

history.meaning: can receive; be able to have someone do

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 貰える

もれる.etymology: Lower bigrade (now ichidan) verb 漏れる・洩れる, continuing Old Japanese *moru* ('to leak out, trickle through a gap, filter through [of light or sound], be omitted').

history.meaning: leak; escape (light, sound, secret); be left out

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 漏れる

もん.etymology: Colloquial phonological reduction of もの (物 'thing; explanatory sentence-final particle'), via apocope of the final vowel (*mono* > *mon*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — もん

や.etymology: Non-exhaustive coordinating particle ('such things as ... and ...') and classical exclamatory/question particle, inherited from Old Japanese *ya*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — や

やすい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yasusi* (安し・易し 'peaceful, calm, easy, effortless'). In Early Modern merchant usage, from 'easy to obtain / worry-free', 安い developed the everyday economic sense 'inexpensive, cheap', while verb-stem + やすい retains the older sense 'easy to do, prone to'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 安い
Wiktionary — やすい (安い・易い) (Japanese)

やっと.etymology: Adverb ('finally, at last; barely, with difficulty'), evolved in Early Modern Japanese by consonant gemination from やっと < やうやう (漸う 'gradually, at long last') or from an interjection of straining effort (やっ + と).

history.meaning: with effort; at long last; barely

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — やっと

やっぱり.etymology: Colloquial emphatic form of やはり (矢張り 'still, after all, just as expected'), formed by consonant gemination (*yahari* > *yappari*). Literally derived from 矢張り ('stretching a rope/arrow taut and keeping it unchanged' -> 'remaining as before, after all').

history.meaning: remaining as before; still; as expected
just as I thought; after all; still

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 矢張り

やる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yaru* (遣る 'to send off, dispatch, propel forward, give to an equal/inferior, perform'). In modern spoken Japanese its sense 'to do, perform, play, try' is ubiquitous alongside its giving sense.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 遣る

やわらかい.etymology: Adjective 柔らかい・軟らかい ('soft, tender, pliant, gentle'), formed by attaching the native *-i* adjective inflection to the Old/Middle Japanese adjectival noun やはらか (*yaparaka* 'soft, gentle', from root *yapa-* 'calm, soft', cognate with 和らぐ *yawaragu*).

history.form: やはらか (柔ら・和らか)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 柔らかい
Wiktionary — やわらかい (柔らかい) (Japanese)

ゆっくり.etymology: Mimetic and manner adverb attested from Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese, formed on the root *yuku-* (related to ゆたか 'abundant, unhurried' and ゆるい 'loose, relaxed') + gemination and *-ri* suffix: 'slowly, unhurriedly, comfortably, at ease'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ゆっくり

よ.etymology: Sentence-final particle inherited from Old Japanese *yo*, originally a vocative and exclamatory particle calling out to the listener. In Modern Japanese it informs, reminds, or emphasizes a point to the addressee ('you know, I tell you').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — よ

よう.etymology: Sino-Japanese formal noun 様 (よう 'manner, way, appearance, kind'), borrowed from Middle Chinese *yangH* (様 'pattern, model, shape, manner'). Also represents the volitional verb suffix -よう (evolved from -う after vowel-stem verbs).

history.meaning: way; manner; so that (~ように); volitional suffix

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 様

ようこそ.etymology: Warm welcoming greeting ('welcome!, how nice that you have come!'), formed in Early Middle Japanese from よう (the *u*-onbin euphonic form of よく 良く 'well, kindly') + emphatic focus particle こそ, elliptical for ようこそおいでくださいました ('you have kindly come indeed').

history.form: やうこそ / ようこそ (良くこそ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ようこそ

ようだ.etymology: Evidential and similative auxiliary ('it seems that, looks like, is like'), formed from the Sino-Japanese formal noun 様 (よう 'appearance, manner') + plain copula だ (replacing classical なり).

history.meaning: seems to be; looks like; is like

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 様だ

ように.etymology: Adverbial and purpose/similative connective ('like, as if, so that, in order to'), formed from the Sino-Japanese formal noun 様 (よう 'manner, way') + dative/adverbial particle に.

history.form: やうに → ように (様に)
history.meaning: in the manner of; so that; in order that

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 様に
Wiktionary — やうに → ように (様に) (Japanese)

よく.etymology: Adverbial (*ren'yōkei*) form of the adjective よい / いい (良い 'good, fine, thorough'), inherited from Old Japanese *yoku* ('well, skillfully, thoroughly, frequently').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 良く

よし.etymology: Exclamation of readiness, resolve, or approval ('all right!, good!, let's do this!'), preserving the classical conclusive (*shūshikei*) form よし (良し・善し 'it is good!') of the adjective よい / いい.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 良し

よね.etymology: Compound sentence-final particle seeking confirmation of shared or inferred knowledge ('isn't that right?, right?'), combining informative よ + rapport/agreement-seeking ね.

history.meaning: right?; isn't it so? (combined sentence-final particle)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — よね

より.etymology: Comparative and ablative case particle ('than, rather than; from'), inherited from Old Japanese *yori* (originally alongside *yuri* / *yu* 'from, through', likely grammaticalized from the verb 寄る / 依る *yoru* 'to lean on, pass by way of').

history.meaning: from; by way of; more than

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — より

よろしい.etymology: Polite adjective 宜しい ('good, fine, acceptable, all right'), continuing Old Japanese *yorosi* ('fitting, well-suited, quite good', derived from the verb 寄る / 依る *yoru* 'to accord with, approach the standard').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 宜しい

よろしく.etymology: Adverbial (*ren'yōkei*) form of よろしい (宜しい 'fitting, good, favorable'), inherited from Old Japanese *yorosiku* ('suitably, favorably'). Used in greeting and request formulas (よろしくお願いします 'please treat me/this favorably').

history.meaning: favorably; please remember me to; pleased to meet you

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 宜しく

ら.etymology: Pluralizing and locative-approximative suffix (-ら 'and others, plural'), inherited from Old Japanese *-ra* (等), where it marked plurality, group association, or approximate location (as in ここら 'around here', 彼ら 'they').

history.meaning: plural, associative, and vague locative suffix

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 等

りんご.etymology: Originally a medieval borrowing of Chinese 林檎 (*línqín*, Middle Chinese *lim gjim*, literally 'forest bird-attracting fruit', referring to the small Asian crabapple *Malus asiatica*). Phonetically shifted from *ringo / rinkin* to りんご, and applied in the Meiji period to large Western apples (*Malus domestica*).

history.form: りんきん / りんご (林檎)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 林檎

りんごジャム.etymology: Hybrid culinary compound ('apple jam'), combining Sino-Japanese/native りんご (林檎 'apple') + English loanword ジャム (from English *jam*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 林檎

る.etymology: Classical passive/potential/spontaneous/honorific auxiliary suffix (-る) inherited from Old Japanese *-ru*, or the non-past conclusive ending (-る) characteristic of ichidan verbs.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — る

れる.etymology: Passive, potential, spontaneous, and honorific auxiliary suffix (-れる, attached to *godan* and *sa-hen* verbs), which evolved in Late Middle Japanese when the classical lower bigrade suffix -る (attributive -るる) shifted to ichidan conjugation (-れる).

history.meaning: passive, spontaneous, potential, and honorific suffix
passive, potential, spontaneous, and honorific suffix

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — れる

わ.etymology: Sentence-final particle expressing emotional realization, mild assertion, or soft emphasis, inherited from Old/Classical Japanese exclamatory particle は (*pa* > *wa*, originally the topic/focus particle shifted to sentence-final position).

history.meaning: soft assertive or emotive sentence-final particle

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — わ

わあ.etymology: Spontaneous native Japanese interjection expressing delight, admiration, amazement, or surprise ('wow!, ooh!'), formed by lengthening the open exclamation わ.

history.meaning: wow!; oh! (exclamation of delight or surprise)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — わあ

わかる.etymology: Inherited from Old/Early Middle Japanese *wakaru* (分かる・判る・解る), originally the intransitive counterpart of わく (分く 'to divide, separate, distinguish'). From 'to become divided or distinct, be sorted out clearly', it shifted in Early Modern Japanese to 'to understand, comprehend, know'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 分かる

わけ.etymology: Verbal noun 訳 ('reason, meaning, circumstances, logical conclusion'), nominalized from the continuative stem of 分ける (*wakeru* 'to divide, distinguish, sort out'). From 'making a clear distinction or analysis of a matter', it came to denote 'sense, reason, grounds'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 訳

わずか.etymology: Adjectival noun and adverb 僅か ('a little, slight, scant, barely'), inherited from Early Middle Japanese *waduka* (originally alongside Old Japanese *wadu-* 'barely, with difficulty').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 僅か

を.etymology: Accusative and perlative case particle (spelled を, pronounced *o*), inherited from Old Japanese *wo*. Originally an emphatic/interjectional particle ('oh, indeed') and object/space-traversed marker, it retained its historical *wa*-row kana spelling を after *wo* merged phonetically with *o*.

history.meaning: emphatic particle; direct object and perlative marker

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — を

ん.etymology: Colloquial syllabic nasal contraction arising in spoken Japanese from either (1) the explanatory nominalizing particle の (*no* > *n* before copulas だ / です), (2) the classical negative auxiliary ぬ (*-nu* > *-n*, as in すみません), or (3) a conversational backchannel ('mm-hmm, yeah').

history.meaning: nominalizer の; negative auxiliary ぬ

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ん

んだ.etymology: Colloquial explanatory sentence-ending construction ('it is that..., the thing is...'), contracted from のだ (*no da*), combining the clause-nominalizing particle の (> ん) + plain copula だ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — のだ

アイシング.etymology: Borrowed from English *icing* ('sugar glaze or frosting applied to pastries and cakes', verbal noun from *ice*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — アイシング

アップライトピアノ.etymology: Borrowed from English *upright piano* ('vertical-stringed piano', from *upright* + *piano*).

history.meaning: piano with vertical strings and soundboard

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — アップライトピアノ
Wiktionary — アップライトピアノ (Japanese)

アーチ.etymology: Borrowed from English *arch* ('curved architectural structure spanning an opening'), ultimately from Old French *arche* and Latin *arcus* ('bow, arch').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — アーチ

アーモンド.etymology: Borrowed from English almond, tracing back through Old French almande to Greek ἀμυγδάλη (amygdálē).
アーモンド.notes: Ground almond meal (アーモンドプードル / アーモンド生地) is prized in Japanese pastry shops for tart crusts.

イニシャル.etymology: Borrowed from English *initial* ('first letter of a name'), ultimately from Latin *initiālis* ('of the beginning', from *initium* 'beginning').

history.meaning: first letter(s) of a person's name

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — イニシャル

インク.etymology: Borrowed from English *ink* (alongside the older Dutch borrowing インキ from Dutch *inkt*), ultimately from Old French *enque* and Late Latin *encaustum*.

history.meaning: colored fluid used for writing and printing

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — インク

ウール.etymology: Borrowed from English *wool* ('fleece of sheep; woolen yarn or cloth'), from Old English *wull*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ウール

エコー.etymology: Borrowed from English *echo* ('reflected sound; reverberation'), from Latin *ēchō* and Ancient Greek ἠχώ (*ēkhō* 'sound, echo').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — エコー

エンジン.etymology: Borrowed from English *engine* ('mechanical motor'), from Old French *engin* and Latin *ingenium* ('innate talent, clever device').

history.meaning: motor converting energy into mechanical motion

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — エンジン

オクターブ.etymology: Borrowed from French/English octave, from Latin octāva ('eighth'), naming the eight-note span of a diatonic scale.
オクターブ.notes: Standard term across Japanese piano instruction and acoustics.

オフィス.etymology: Borrowed from English *office* ('place of business, workroom'), from Anglo-Norman/Old French *office* and Latin *officium* ('duty, service, office').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オフィス

オリーブオイル.etymology: Compound loanword from English olive oil (オリーブ + オイル).
オリーブオイル.notes: Coexists with older Sino-hybrid オリーブ油 (オリーブゆ) in home cooking and cafés.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オレンジジュース
Wiktionary — オレンジジュース (Japanese)

オーナー.etymology: Borrowed from English *owner* ('proprietor, one who owns a business or property', agent noun from *own*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オーナー

オーブン.etymology: Borrowed from English *oven* ('enclosed heated chamber for baking and roasting'), from Old English *ofn*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オーブン

オープン.etymology: Borrowed from English *open* ('unclosed, open for business, newly opened'), from Old English *open*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オープン

カウンター.etymology: Borrowed from English *counter* ('long table or bar surface in a shop, café, or kitchen where customers are served'), from Anglo-Norman *countour* ('counting-house desk') and Latin *computāre*.

history.meaning: counter (in a café, bakery, or reception)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カウンター

カウントダウン.etymology: Borrowed from English *countdown* ('counting backward to zero to mark the start of an event', from *count* + *down*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カウントダウン

カチッ.etymology: Onomatopoeic adverb written in katakana with a final glottal stop (ッ), imitating the crisp, metallic or hard-plastic click of a latch, timer, or switch engaging ('click!, snap!').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — かちっと

カチッと.etymology: Onomatopoeic adverb formed from カチッ ('click!') + quotative/adverbial particle と, describing a switch, lock, or mechanism clicking cleanly into place ('with a crisp click').

history.meaning: with a sharp click; firmly in place

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — かちっと
Wiktionary — カチッと (かちっと) (Japanese)

カップ.etymology: Borrowed from English *cup* ('small handled drinking vessel for tea or coffee; measuring cup'), from Late Latin *cuppa* ('drinking vessel'). Contrasts in Japanese with コップ (from Dutch/Portuguese *kop*, usually a handleless glass tumbler).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カップ

カフェ.etymology: Borrowed from French café ('coffeehouse'), first popularized in late Meiji and Taishō cities and revived in contemporary Japanese for neighborhood coffeehouses.

カモミールティー.etymology: Compound loanword from English *chamomile tea* (combining *chamomile*, from Greek χαμαίμηλον *khamaimēlon* 'earth-apple', + *tea*).

history.meaning: herbal infusion made from chamomile flowers

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カモミール

カーテン.etymology: Borrowed from English *curtain* ('hanging window drapery'), from Old French *cortine* and Late Latin *cortīna*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カーテン

カーディガン.etymology: Borrowed from English *cardigan* ('knitted sweater opening down the front with buttons'), named after James Brudenell, 7th Earl of Cardigan (1797–1868), whose troops wore knitted waistcoats during the Crimean War.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カーディガン

カード.etymology: Borrowed from English *card* ('stiff rectangular piece of paper or plastic'), from Old French *carte* and Latin *charta* ('papyrus leaf, paper').

history.meaning: message card, index card, or payment card

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カード

ガラス.etymology: Borrowed in the Edo period from Dutch glas ('glass'), referring to sheet and window glass as a material (whereas the later English borrowing グラス denotes a drinking glass).

ガラス瓶.etymology: Hybrid compound noun ガラス瓶 ('glass bottle, glass jar'), combining Edo-period Dutch loanword ガラス (from Dutch *glas* 'glass') + Sino-Japanese 瓶 (びん 'bottle, jar', from Middle Chinese *beng*).

history.form: ガラス (硝子) + 瓶 (びん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 硝子瓶

ガーデンカフェ.etymology: Compound loanword combining English *garden* (ガーデン) + French/English *café* (カフェ), referring to a café with an outdoor garden terrace.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カフェ

キッチン.etymology: Borrowed from English *kitchen* ('room equipped for preparing and cooking food'), from Old English *cyċene* and Vulgar Latin *cocīna*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — キッチン

クッション.etymology: Borrowed from English cushion, from Old French coissin.
クッション.notes: Refers to soft seat cushions on wooden café chairs as well as mechanical shock-absorbing pads.

クリーム色.etymology: Hybrid color compound クリーム色 ('cream color, pale yellowish-white'), combining English loanword クリーム (from English *cream*) + native Japanese 色 (いろ 'color, hue').

history.meaning: pale yellowish-white color of dairy cream

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — クリーム色
Wiktionary — クリーム + 色 (いろ) (Japanese)

クルミ材.etymology: Hybrid woodworking compound クルミ材 ('walnut wood, walnut timber'), combining native Japanese クルミ (胡桃 'walnut tree') + Sino-Japanese 材 (ざい 'timber, lumber, material').

history.form: クルミ (胡桃) + 材 (ざい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 胡桃

クロス.etymology: Borrowed from two converging English words: (1) English *cloth* ('woven fabric, tablecloth', as in テーブルクロス), and (2) English *cross* ('intersecting lines, cross shape'). In café and interior contexts it commonly denotes a tablecloth or wiping cloth.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — クロス

グラニュー糖.etymology: Hybrid Meiji culinary compound clipping English granulated (sugar) to グラニュー and attaching Sino-Japanese 糖 (とう, 'sugar').
グラニュー糖.notes: Refers to fine, dry, free-flowing white crystals prized in pastry baking.

コク.etymology: Culinary and sensory noun コク (originally written 濃く or 酷 'richness, body, depth of flavor'), derived from the Sino-Japanese noun 酷 (*koku* 'intense, ripe to the fullest degree', or the adverbial stem 濃く *koku* of 濃い 'thick, rich, strong'). Often written in katakana in modern food writing.

history.meaning: full-bodied ripeness and depth of taste in sake or broth

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — こく

コップ.etymology: Borrowed from Dutch kop (or Portuguese copo) during the early modern trade era to name a tumbler or drinking cup without a handle.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コンサートホール
Wiktionary — コンサートホール (Japanese)

コンロ.etymology: Edo-period Sino-Japanese kitchen word 焜炉 (こんろ, combining 焜 'bright flame' + 炉 'hearth/brazier'), influenced in use by Dutch komfoor ('portable brazier').
コンロ.notes: Today written in katakana コンロ for gas and induction kitchen stoves.

コート.etymology: Borrowed from English *coat* ('outer garment worn for warmth; layer of paint/glaze'), from Old French *cote* ('tunic, coat'); or homophonous English *court* ('sports court').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コート

コーナー.etymology: Borrowed from English *corner* ('angle where two walls or streets meet; specialized section in a shop or room'), from Anglo-Norman *cornere* and Latin *cornū* ('horn, projecting point').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コーナー

コーヒー.etymology: Borrowed in the late Edo period from Dutch koffie ('coffee') through the Dutch trading post at Dejima in Nagasaki; scholars also coined the phonetic kanji spelling 珈琲.

コーヒーカップ.etymology: Borrowed from English *coffee cup* (combining Dutch/English loanword コーヒー 'coffee' + English カップ 'cup').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コーヒーカップ

コーヒーマシン.etymology: Borrowed from English *coffee machine* (combining コーヒー 'coffee' + English マシン 'machine, automated appliance').

history.meaning: appliance for brewing espresso or coffee

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コーヒー

サイズ.etymology: Borrowed from English *size* ('dimensions, magnitude, garment/portion measurement'), shortened in Middle English from *assize* ('fixed standard or measure', from Old French *assise*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — サイズ
